docs.title: Automate with access tokens
docs.description: Choose between a personal and an organization access token, pick scopes and an expiry, store the secret safely, and revoke it when you're done.
docs.body:
An **access token** is a long random secret that starts with `flagon_` and authenticates a
script, CI job, or MCP client to the Flagon API. You send it as a bearer token:
`Authorization: Bearer flagon_...`. Every token has two limits: the **role** of whoever it acts
as (a token can never do more than its principal), and optional **scopes** that narrow it
further to specific kinds of operations.

By the end of this guide you will have a token with only the access your automation needs, a
way to check what it can do, and a plan for rotating and revoking it.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Personal access token:** any signed-in user.
- **Organization access token:** organization **owner** or **admin**.
- **Tokens are managed in the dashboard only.** Creating, listing, and revoking tokens is not
  available through a token, the assistant, or MCP, so a leaked token can't mint more tokens.

</Callout>

## Personal or organization token?

| | Personal access token (PAT) | Organization access token (OAT) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prefix | `flagon_pat_` | `flagon_oat_` |
| Acts as | You | A service principal that belongs to the organization, named after the token |
| Reaches | Every organization you belong to, with your role in each | Only its own organization |
| Role | Yours | Chosen at creation: `admin`, `member`, or `viewer` (read-only) |
| Created in | Personal **Settings > Personal access tokens** | Organization **Settings > API tokens** |
| When a person leaves | Stops being able to reach that organization | Unaffected; it isn't tied to a person |
| Audit log actor | You | The token's name |

Use an **organization token** for shared automation such as CI: it survives people changing
jobs, it can't reach other organizations, and its changes are attributed to the automation.
Use a **personal token** for your own scripts and your own MCP client.

## Scopes

A token with **Full access** is limited only by its role. Otherwise, pick scopes; a parent scope
includes its children.

| Group | Scopes, broadest first | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account | `admin:user` > `user` > `read:user` | Your profile. |
| Organizations | `admin:org` > `write:org` > `read:org` | `read:org`: organizations, members, invitations, security policy, SSO providers, audit log. `write:org`: manage those. `admin:org`: create, leave, delete, restore organizations. |
| Projects | `admin:project` > `write:project` > `read:project` | `write:project`: create and edit projects. `admin:project`: delete and restore, and manage collaborators, team grants, and owners. |
| Teams | `admin:team` > `write:team` > `read:team` | `write:team`: create and edit teams and their members. `admin:team`: delete teams. |
| Notifications | `notifications` | Your notifications. |

See the [scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes) for the operation-by-operation map.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create the token">

**Personal token:** open personal **Settings > Personal access tokens** and select
**Generate new token**.

**Organization token:** open organization **Settings > API tokens** (under **Developer**) and
select **Generate new token**. The button appears only for owners and admins.

On the form:

1. **Token name**: something you'll recognize later, such as `github-actions-deploy`.
2. **Role** (organization tokens only): `Admin`, `Member`, or `Viewer`. The token can never
   exceed it.
3. **Expiration**: **7 days**, **30 days** (the default), **90 days**, **1 year**, **Custom...**
   (pick a date), or **No expiration**.
4. **Permissions**: check **Full access**, or check only the scopes you need.
5. Select **Generate token**.

</Step>

<Step title="Copy the secret once">

The next screen says **Token created. Copy it now.** and shows the full secret with a **Copy**
button. This is the only time it is shown: Flagon stores only a hash, and lists show just a
short prefix such as `flagon_pat_ab12cd`. Put it straight into a secret store, such as your CI
provider's encrypted secrets or a password manager. Never commit it.

</Step>

<Step title="Verify what it can do">

```bash
export FLAGON_TOKEN=flagon_pat_...
curl https://api.flagon.io/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

`GET /me` (needs `read:user`) returns who the token acts as and its organizations. For an
organization token, that is the service principal and its one organization. Then call an
endpoint your automation needs, for example `GET /orgs/acme/projects` with `read:project`.

</Step>

<Step title="Rotate and revoke">

Each row in the token list shows its access, **Last used**, and **Expires**. To rotate, create
a new token, switch your automation to it, then revoke the old one: select **Revoke** on its
row and confirm with **Revoke token**. Revocation takes effect on the next request. Revoking
an organization token also removes its service principal from the organization.

An expired token is rejected the same way as a revoked one. Organization tokens also stop
working when their organization is deleted.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | `invalid or expired token` | The token is wrong, revoked, or expired, or its organization was deleted. |
| `403` | `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` | Add the scope (create a new token; scopes can't be edited). |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | The scope is there, but the token's role doesn't allow the action. |
| `403` | `this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue` | A personal access token whose user has no 2FA, in an organization that requires it. Organization tokens are exempt. |
| `403` | `this organization requires single sign-on; sign in through the organization's identity provider at least once before using a personal access token with it` | The organization requires SSO and the token's user has never signed in through its provider. Owners and organization tokens are exempt. |
| `403` | `this operation requires a user; organization access tokens can't perform it` | Organization tokens can't create, leave, or restore organizations, list deleted organizations, or sync a profile. Use a personal token. |
| `404` | `organization not found` | The token's principal isn't a member of that organization. An organization token can only reach its own. |
| `422` | `select at least one scope, or choose full access` | Shown on the create form if you pick nothing. |
| `422` | `expiration must be in the future` | Pick a later custom date. |

Over MCP, the same problems come back as a JSON-RPC error `-32001` (`invalid or expired token`)
or `-32003` (missing scope).

- [Tokens and scopes](/docs/security/tokens-and-scopes)

docs.title: Call the API from CI
docs.description: Store an organization access token as a CI secret and call the Flagon API from a pipeline, with a complete GitHub Actions example that syncs a project's README.
headings: Other calls a pipeline often makes
docs.body:
Anything you can do in the dashboard is an API operation, so a CI pipeline can keep Flagon in
step with your repository. The pattern is always the same: create an **organization access
token** with only the scopes the job needs, store it as an encrypted CI secret, and call
`https://api.flagon.io` with it as a bearer token.

By the end of this guide you will have a GitHub Actions workflow that, on every push to `main`,
checks that its token works and publishes the repository's `README.md` to the matching Flagon
project. The same steps work in any CI system that can run `curl`.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner** or **admin**, to create the organization token.
- **A project** to sync, for example `checkout` in the `acme` organization. See
  [Create a project](/docs/guides/create-a-project).
- **Token:** an organization access token with the scope `write:project` (which includes
  `read:project`). Editing a project needs an effective `write` role on it. A token with role
  **Member** gets the organization's [base permission](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions)
  (default `read`), which is not enough; a token with role **Admin** has `admin` on every
  project. The scope still limits what an Admin token can do: with only `write:project` it can
  read, create, and edit projects, and nothing else.

</Callout>

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create a narrowly scoped organization token">

In organization **Settings > API tokens**, select **Generate new token**. Name it after the job
(`checkout-readme-sync`), choose role **Admin** (or **Member** if your base permission is
`write` or higher), an expiration you will actually rotate (for
example **90 days**), and check only `write:project`. Copy the secret; it is shown once. See
[Automate with access tokens](/docs/guides/automate-with-access-tokens) for details.

</Step>

<Step title="Store it as a CI secret">

In your GitHub repository, go to **Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions** and add a
repository secret named `FLAGON_TOKEN` with the token as its value. GitHub masks the value in
logs. Other CI systems have an equivalent encrypted variable; never put the token in the
repository or the workflow file.

</Step>

<Step title="Add the workflow">

Save this as `.github/workflows/flagon.yml`:

```yaml
name: Sync to Flagon

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: [README.md]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  sync-readme:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      FLAGON_API: https://api.flagon.io
      FLAGON_ORG: acme
      FLAGON_PROJECT: checkout
      FLAGON_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLAGON_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check the token can see the project
        run: |
          curl --fail-with-body -sS \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
            -H "User-Agent: flagon-ci/${{ github.repository }}" \
            "$FLAGON_API/orgs/$FLAGON_ORG/projects/$FLAGON_PROJECT" \
            | jq '{name, slug, updated_at}'

      - name: Publish README.md to the project
        run: |
          jq -Rs '{readme: .}' README.md > body.json
          curl --fail-with-body -sS -X PATCH \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "User-Agent: flagon-ci/${{ github.repository }}" \
            --data @body.json \
            "$FLAGON_API/orgs/$FLAGON_ORG/projects/$FLAGON_PROJECT" \
            | jq '{slug, updated_at}'
```

What each part does:

- `--fail-with-body` makes `curl` exit non-zero on a `4xx` or `5xx` while still printing the
  error body, so the step fails and the log shows Flagon's `detail` message.
- `jq -Rs '{readme: .}'` reads the whole file as one string and builds valid JSON, so quotes and
  newlines in the README can't break the request.
- `PATCH` changes only the fields you send; here, just `readme`.
- A descriptive `User-Agent` is recorded in the organization's audit log for each change, which
  makes CI-driven changes easy to spot.

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- Push a README change to `main` (or run the workflow manually). Both steps pass, and the second
  prints the project's new `updated_at`.
- The project's **Overview** shows the new README.
- The organization's audit log records `project.updated` with the token's name as the actor.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Other calls a pipeline often makes

| Goal | Request | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create the project if it doesn't exist | `POST /orgs/{slug}/projects` with `{"name": "...", "slug": "..."}`; treat `409` as "already exists" | `write:project` |
| Read project metadata | `GET /orgs/{slug}/projects/{project}` | `read:project` |
| List projects | `GET /orgs/{slug}/projects?limit=100`, following the `Link` header | `read:project` |
| Export the audit log | `GET /orgs/{slug}/audit`, following the `Link` header | `read:org`, token role `admin` |

Paths in the table use `{slug}` and `{project}` as placeholders. The full, generated contract is
at `https://api.flagon.io/openapi.json`; see [OpenAPI](/docs/api/openapi).

## Troubleshooting

| Status | `detail` | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | `invalid or expired token` | The secret is wrong, revoked, or expired. Create a new token and update `FLAGON_TOKEN`. |
| `403` | `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` | Create a token with the scope in the table above. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | The token's role gives it less than `write` on the project. Use an Admin token, or raise the base permission. |
| `404` | `project not found` | Check `FLAGON_ORG` and `FLAGON_PROJECT`, and that the token can see the project. |
| `413` | `request body is too large` | The body is over the API's request size cap (4 MiB by default). Very large READMEs won't fit. |
| `422` | `validation failed` | The body isn't what the operation expects. Print `body.json` to check it. |
| `429` | `rate limit exceeded; retry after Ns` | The token sent requests faster than the API's per-token limit. Wait for the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then retry. |
| `5xx` | a generic message | A server-side failure. Retry, and quote the response's `X-Request-Id` header if you report it. |

## Related

- [Automate with access tokens](/docs/guides/automate-with-access-tokens)
- [Using the API](/docs/api/using-the-api)
- [Errors](/docs/api/errors)
- [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination)

docs.title: Connect an MCP client
docs.description: Point Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any other MCP client at mcp.flagon.io, authenticate with an access token, and check which tools it can use.
docs.body:
Flagon runs a **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server, so an AI agent outside Flagon, such as the
assistant in your editor, can read Flagon's documentation and operate your organizations. It
exposes the same tool registry as the in-product assistant, and every tool calls the same
permission-checked operation as the REST API, so an MCP client can never do more than you could
in the dashboard.

By the end of this guide your MCP client will list Flagon's tools, and you will be able to ask
it things like "list the projects in acme" and have it act as you.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **An MCP client** that can connect to a remote HTTP server, or can run the `mcp-remote` bridge
  with Node.js.
- **An access token** for anything beyond the docs. A personal access token acts as you across
  your organizations; an organization token reaches only its organization. See
  [Automate with access tokens](/docs/guides/automate-with-access-tokens).

</Callout>

## What the server speaks

| | |
| --- | --- |
| URL | `https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp` (the root, `https://mcp.flagon.io`, serves the same endpoint) |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP, `POST` only. Each JSON-RPC 2.0 request gets a single JSON response; the server does not open a server-sent events stream, and `GET` returns `405`. |
| Protocol version | `2024-11-05`, returned by `initialize` |
| Methods | `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` |
| Auth | Optional `Authorization: Bearer flagon_...` header |

## What you can reach

| Caller | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| No token | `search_docs` and `get_doc` only, over public documentation. |
| Token with full access | Every tool, bounded by the token's role. |
| Scoped token | The docs tools, plus each tool whose scope the token holds. Tools it can't use are not listed. |

Internal documentation pages (none today) are returned to any caller with a valid token, and
never to an anonymous one. The [tool reference](/docs/ai/tools) lists each tool with its scope.

A tool call that names an organization also passes that organization's security policy: with a
personal access token, an organization that requires two-factor authentication or SSO refuses
the call (as a tool result with `"isError": true`) until the token's user meets the requirement.
Organization access tokens are exempt. Changes made over MCP are recorded in the audit log with
your client's IP address and `User-Agent`.

<Callout type="warn" title="Mutations run when your client calls them">

In the dashboard, the assistant proposes every change and waits for you to confirm. Over MCP,
Flagon runs a tool as soon as the client calls it; any confirmation step is your MCP client's
own tool-approval prompt. Keep your client's approval prompts on for Flagon, and use a scoped,
read-only token (for example `read:org` and `read:project`) when you only need answers.

</Callout>

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create a token">

In personal **Settings > Personal access tokens**, generate a token. For a read-only agent,
check `read:org`, `read:project`, and `read:team`. Copy the secret and export it in your shell:

```bash
export FLAGON_TOKEN=flagon_pat_...
```

</Step>

<Step title="Add Flagon to your client">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Claude Code">

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http flagon https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

Run `/mcp` inside Claude Code to confirm `flagon` is connected.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Claude Desktop">

Claude Desktop's config file launches local servers, so use the `mcp-remote` bridge (requires
Node.js). Edit `claude_desktop_config.json` (**Settings > Developer > Edit Config**):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "flagon": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp",
        "--header",
        "Authorization:${FLAGON_AUTH}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "FLAGON_AUTH": "Bearer flagon_pat_..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The header is passed through an environment variable, with no space after the colon, so the
space inside `Bearer flagon_...` doesn't break argument parsing. Restart Claude Desktop after
saving.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Cursor">

Add Flagon to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "flagon": {
      "url": "https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:FLAGON_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`${env:FLAGON_TOKEN}` reads the token from your environment, so it stays out of the file. Check
the server's status under Cursor's MCP settings.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Other clients">

Any client that supports remote Streamable HTTP servers needs the URL
`https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp` and the header `Authorization: Bearer <your token>`. A generic
configuration usually looks like:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "flagon": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer flagon_pat_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

Field names vary by client (`type`, `transport`, `serverUrl`); check its documentation. Clients
that only speak stdio can use the `mcp-remote` bridge shown in the Claude Desktop tab.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify the connection">

Ask your client "which Flagon tools do you have?", or call the server directly:

```bash
curl -sS https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"}' \
  | jq '.result.tools[].name'
```

Without the header you should see only `search_docs` and `get_doc`. Then try a real call:

```bash
curl -sS https://mcp.flagon.io/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call",
       "params": {"name": "list_projects", "arguments": {"org": "acme"}}}'
```

The result is a single text block containing JSON. Organization-scoped tools take the
organization slug as `org`.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Errors

MCP errors arrive as JSON-RPC errors in an HTTP `200` response, or as a tool result with
`"isError": true`:

| Code or result | Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-32001` | `invalid or expired token` | The token didn't resolve. Flagon rejects it rather than silently treating you as anonymous. |
| `-32003` | `this token is missing the scope required for <tool>` | Use a token with that tool's scope. |
| `-32602` | `unknown tool: <name>` | The tool doesn't exist, or you're anonymous and it needs a token. |
| `-32602` | `invalid params` | The `tools/call` params are malformed. |
| `-32601` | `method not found: <method>` | The server implements only the methods listed above. |
| `-32700` | `parse error` | The request body isn't valid JSON. |
| `"isError": true` | For example `project not found` | The operation failed with the same message the REST API returns. |

HTTP `405` means the client sent a `GET`; this server only accepts `POST`. HTTP `413` means the
request body was over the API's size cap, and HTTP `429` (with a `Retry-After` header) means the
token sent requests faster than the per-token rate limit.

## Related

- [MCP server](/docs/ai/mcp)
- [Tool reference](/docs/ai/tools)
- [Automate with access tokens](/docs/guides/automate-with-access-tokens)
- [Troubleshooting the assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp)

docs.title: Create a project
docs.description: Create a project in your organization, give it a README and repository link, and confirm it from the dashboard or the API.
docs.body:
A **project** is the core unit in Flagon: one deployable app or service, with a name, a URL
slug, a one-line description, a Markdown README, and a link to its source repository. Access
to a project is controlled per project (see
[Manage project access](/docs/guides/manage-project-access)), and every change to it lands in the
organization's audit log.

By the end of this guide you will have a project at `app.flagon.io/<org>/projects/<slug>`,
with a README, that teammates can open according to their access.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner**, **admin**, or **member** to create a project. Editing it
  afterwards needs an effective `write` role on that project, and renaming its slug needs
  `maintain`. If you are a member, Flagon grants you `admin` on the project you create.
- **API token scope:** `write:project` (which includes `read:project`).

</Callout>

<Callout type="note" title="Deployments are not built yet">

A project today holds metadata, a README, and access control. The **Deployments** and
**Activity** tabs on a project are placeholders for features that have not shipped. See
[Deployments](/docs/deploying/deployments) for the plan.

</Callout>

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create the project">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open **Projects** in the sidebar and select **New project**.
2. Fill in **Project name** (for example, `Checkout Service`). The **Slug** is derived from the
   name; edit it if you want a different URL.
3. Optionally add a **Description** (one line) and a **Repository URL**.
4. Select **Create project**. Flagon opens the project's **Overview**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Checkout Service",
    "slug": "checkout",
    "description": "Takes payments and places orders",
    "repository_url": "https://github.com/acme/checkout",
    "readme": "# Checkout\n\nOwned by the payments team."
  }'
```

Only `name` is required; `slug` is derived from it when omitted. A `201 Created` returns the
project:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://api.flagon.io/schemas/Project.json",
  "id": "0d9a...",
  "org_id": "6f1c...",
  "name": "Checkout Service",
  "slug": "checkout",
  "description": "Takes payments and places orders",
  "readme": "# Checkout\n\nOwned by the payments team.",
  "repository_url": "https://github.com/acme/checkout",
  "created_by": "u_123",
  "created_at": "2026-09-25T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-25T12:00:00Z"
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Create a project called Checkout Service in acme, linked to https://github.com/acme/checkout.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Create project "Checkout Service" in "acme"** and creates it
after you select **Confirm**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Add a README">

The README is Markdown and renders on the project's **Overview** tab.

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Open the project and edit the README from the **Overview** tab. Name, slug, description, and
repository URL live under the project's **Settings > General**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

`PATCH` changes only the fields you send:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"readme": "# Checkout\n\nRuns on Postgres. On call: #payments."}'
```

Sending `slug` renames the project and changes its URL; that needs an effective `maintain` role
on the project, while the other fields need `write`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Update the checkout project's description to "Payments and order placement".

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- The project appears on **Projects**, and its page loads at `app.flagon.io/acme/projects/checkout`.
- `GET /orgs/acme/projects/checkout` returns it. Add `?expand[]=organization` to inline the
  organization object in the response.
- `GET /orgs/acme/projects` lists it inside `{"projects": [...]}`. Lists are paginated with
  `limit` and a `cursor` from the `Link` header; see [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).
- The audit log records `project.created`, and `project.updated` for each edit.

</Step>

<Step title="Decide who can reach it">

Right after creation, access follows the organization's
[base permission](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions): with the default `read`, every member can
see the project. The creator is the exception: a member who creates a project gets a direct
`admin` grant on it (recorded in the audit log as `project.access_granted`), so they can manage
its access even when the base permission is `read` or `none`. Org owners and admins already hold
`admin` and the owner tier on every project. Creating a project does not make you its owner, so
deleting it still takes an owner. To grant people or teams more, or to add owners, see
[Manage project access](/docs/guides/manage-project-access) and
[Transfer project ownership](/docs/guides/transfer-project-ownership).

</Step>

</Steps>

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `a project with that slug already exists` | Slugs are unique among live projects in the organization. Pick another, or restore or rename the existing one. |
| `422` | `name is required and must contain a letter or digit` | Send a non-empty `name`. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | Your organization role can't create projects (a legacy viewer, or an organization access token with the viewer role), or your project role is below `write` for edits or below `maintain` for a slug rename. |
| `404` | `project not found` | The slug is wrong, the project was deleted, or you have no access to it. |
| `403` | `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` | Use a token with `write:project`. |

## Related

- [Projects](/docs/platform/projects)
- [Manage project access](/docs/guides/manage-project-access)
- [Delete and restore](/docs/guides/delete-and-restore)
- [Expanding responses](/docs/api/expanding-responses)

docs.title: Create an organization
docs.description: Create the organization that holds your projects, teams, and members, from the dashboard, the API, or the assistant.
docs.body:
An **organization** is the workspace everything else in Flagon lives in: projects, teams,
members, access tokens, security settings, and the audit log. Every dashboard URL starts with
the organization's slug (`app.flagon.io/acme/...`), and every domain API call names it
(`/orgs/acme/...`). Your personal account settings at `/settings` are the only thing outside an
organization.

By the end of this guide you will own a new organization, reachable at
`app.flagon.io/<slug>`, and know how to confirm it exists from the API.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Account:** a verified Flagon account. Anyone with an account can create an organization;
  there is no role requirement because you become its **owner**.
- **Plan limit:** the free plan includes **one organization that you own**. Being a member of
  other people's organizations is unlimited. Organizations you deleted do not count toward the
  limit while they sit in your recently deleted archive.
- **API token (optional):** to create one from the API, a personal access token with the
  `admin:org` scope (or full access). Organization access tokens cannot create organizations.

</Callout>

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Pick a name and a slug">

The **name** is the display label (`Acme Inc`). The **slug** is the URL segment (`acme-inc`) and
must be unique across Flagon. Flagon normalizes a slug to lowercase letters, digits, and single
hyphens: `Acme Inc` becomes `acme-inc`. If you don't give a slug, Flagon derives it from the name.

A name must contain at least one letter or digit, or the request fails with `422` and
`name is required and must contain a letter or digit`.

</Step>

<Step title="Create the organization">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Go to [app.flagon.io/new](https://app.flagon.io/new). A new account is sent here
   automatically after email verification.
2. Enter an **Organization name**. The form previews the URL it derives, for example
   `app.flagon.io/acme-inc`.
3. Select **Create organization**. Flagon opens the new organization's dashboard.

The dashboard derives the slug from the name. To choose a slug that differs from the name, use
the API or the assistant.

If you already own an organization, this page shows **You've reached the free plan limit**
instead of the form.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Acme Inc", "slug": "acme"}'
```

A `201 Created` response returns the organization, with your role in it:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://api.flagon.io/schemas/Org.json",
  "id": "6f1c...",
  "name": "Acme Inc",
  "slug": "acme",
  "role": "owner",
  "enforce_two_factor": false,
  "require_sso": false,
  "created_at": "2026-09-25T12:00:00Z"
}
```

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

Open **Ask AI** in any organization you already belong to and ask:

> Create an organization called Acme Inc.

The assistant proposes the change as a card reading
**Confirm: Create organization "Acme Inc"**. Nothing happens until you select **Confirm**. See
[Work with the assistant](/docs/guides/work-with-the-assistant) for how proposals work.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

In the dashboard, the organization switcher in the sidebar now lists the new organization, and
**Settings > Organizations** (your personal settings) shows it with the **Owner** role.

From the API, list the organizations you belong to:

```bash
curl https://api.flagon.io/orgs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

The response is `{"orgs": [...]}` and includes the new slug with `"role": "owner"`. Creating
the organization also writes an `organization.created` entry to its
[audit log](/docs/guides/review-the-audit-log) and sends you a welcome notification.

</Step>

<Step title="Set it up">

A new organization has only you in it. Typical next steps:

- [Invite your team](/docs/guides/invite-your-team).
- [Set base permissions](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions) so members get the right default
  access to projects.
- [Create a project](/docs/guides/create-a-project).

To rename the organization later, go to **Settings > General**, or call
`PATCH /orgs/{slug}` with `{"name": "New name"}` (owners and admins, `write:org` scope). The
slug cannot be changed after creation.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `402` | `the free plan includes one organization; add a payment method to create more` | You already own one live organization. Paid plans are not available yet, so delete or hand over ownership of the existing one, or ask to be added to someone else's organization. |
| `409` | `that org slug is already taken` | Pick another slug. Slugs are unique across all of Flagon, not just your account. |
| `422` | `name is required and must contain a letter or digit` | Send a non-empty `name`. |
| `403` | `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` | Your token lacks `admin:org`. Create a token with that scope. |
| `403` | `this operation requires a user; organization access tokens can't perform it` | You used an organization access token. Use a personal access token. |

## Related

- [Organizations](/docs/platform/organizations)
- [Invite your team](/docs/guides/invite-your-team)
- [Delete and restore](/docs/guides/delete-and-restore)
- [Errors](/docs/api/errors)

docs.title: Delete and restore
docs.description: Soft-delete a project or an organization, restore it later, and handle a slug that was taken while it was gone.
headings: List deleted projects (paginated; organization owners and admins)
docs.body:
Deleting in Flagon is a **soft delete**: the project or organization disappears from every list
and URL straight away, but its data, settings, and access grants are kept so it can be restored.
Its slug is freed immediately, so you can reuse the name for something new. That last point is
why restores sometimes need a decision: if a new project or organization took the slug in the
meantime, the old one comes back under a new slug you choose. Both projects and organizations
can be restored for **30 days** after they are deleted.

By the end of this guide you will be able to delete a project or an organization, bring it back,
and resolve the slug conflicts and plan limits that can block a restore.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Projects:** the owner tier on the project: an organization **owner** or **admin**, a project
  owner, or a member of a team that owns it. Token scope `admin:project`.
- **Organizations:** organization **owner** only. Token scope `admin:org`.

</Callout>

## Projects

<Steps>

<Step title="Delete the project">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open the project, then **Settings > General**.
2. In **Danger zone**, select **Delete project**.
3. Type the project's slug to confirm, and select **Delete project**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

The response is the project as it was deleted.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Delete the checkout project.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Delete project "checkout" in "acme"**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Restore it">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Open organization **Settings > Deleted projects** (under **Archive**; owners and admins), find
the project, and select **Restore**. Each row shows how many days it stays restorable. It comes
back with its settings and access intact.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
# List deleted projects (paginated; organization owners and admins)
curl https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/deleted-projects \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
# {"projects": [{"slug": "checkout", ..., "deleted_at": "...", "purge_at": "..."}]}

# Restore by slug
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout/restore \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

`purge_at` is when the project stops being restorable (30 days after `deleted_at`). If several
deleted projects share the slug (it was reused and deleted again), restore brings back the most
recently deleted one. The list is limited to organization owners and admins; a project owner who
is neither can still restore by slug.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Restore the checkout project.

The assistant can look it up with `list_deleted_projects` and proposes
**Confirm: Restore project "checkout" in "acme"** (with `as "checkout-2"` added when it restores
under a new slug).

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="If the slug was taken">

A restore under the old slug fails with `409` and
`that project slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` when a live project now uses the
slug. Restore it under a different slug instead:

- **Dashboard:** after **Restore**, a dialog asks for a **New slug** (it suggests
  `<slug>-2`). Links to the old slug won't reach the restored project.
- **API:** send the new slug in the optional request body.
- **Assistant:** ask it to restore the project under a new slug; the `restore_project` tool
  takes a `new_slug`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout/restore \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug": "checkout-2"}'
```

</Step>

</Steps>

After 30 days a deleted project is no longer listed and can't be restored: restore returns
`404` with `no restorable project with that slug`.

## Organizations

<Steps>

<Step title="Delete the organization">

Deleting an organization removes it for **every member at once**, stops its projects being
reachable, stops its organization access tokens from authenticating, and frees its slug. Every
member is notified. An owner can restore it for **30 days**.

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open organization **Settings > General**. The **Danger zone** appears only for owners.
2. Select **Delete organization**.
3. Type the organization's slug to confirm, and select **Delete organization**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

Use a personal access token: organization access tokens can't hold the owner role.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Delete the acme organization.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Delete organization "acme" (restorable by an owner for 30
days)**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Restore it within 30 days">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open your personal **Settings > Organizations**. The **Recently deleted** table lists
   organizations you owned, with how long each stays restorable.
2. Select **Restore**.
3. If the old slug was taken meanwhile, a dialog asks for a **New slug**. Enter one and select
   **Restore organization**. Links to the old slug won't reach the restored organization.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

The archive and restore address an organization by **id**, because its old slug may now belong
to someone else:

```bash
curl https://api.flagon.io/deleted-orgs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
# {"orgs": [{"id": "6f1c...", "name": "Acme Inc", "slug": "acme",
#            "deleted_at": "...", "purge_at": "..."}]}

curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/deleted-orgs/6f1c.../restore \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug": "acme-2"}'
```

The body is optional; send `slug` only when the old one is taken. `purge_at` is when the
organization stops being restorable.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

The in-product assistant can list your deleted organizations with `list_deleted_organizations`,
but it refuses to restore one: each conversation is scoped to a single organization, and a
deleted organization is addressed by id from outside it. Restore from the dashboard or the API.

An external agent connected over [MCP](/docs/guides/connect-an-mcp-client) with a personal
access token that has `admin:org` can call `restore_organization` with the `id` (and a new
`slug` if needed).

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Check the plan limit">

A deleted organization does not count toward the free plan's one owned organization, which is
why you could create a new one after deleting. Restoring counts it again: if you already own a
live organization, the restore fails with `402`. Delete or hand over the other organization
first; paid plans are not available yet.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Verify it worked

- A deleted project or organization no longer appears in lists, and its URLs return a not-found
  page.
- A restored one reappears at its slug (or its new slug) with its members, projects, teams, and
  grants as they were.
- The audit log records `project.deleted` and `project.restored`, or `organization.deleted` and
  `organization.restored`.

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `403` | `only an organization owner can delete it` | Ask an owner. |
| `403` | `only an organization owner can restore it` | Ask an owner. |
| `404` | `no restorable organization with that id` | The id is wrong, you did not own it, or the 30 days have passed. |
| `409` | `that org slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Send a new `slug` in the restore body. |
| `402` | `the free plan includes one organization; add a payment method to restore another` | You already own a live organization. |
| `409` | `that project slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Send a new `slug` in the restore body. |
| `404` | `no restorable project with that slug` | No project with that slug was deleted in this organization in the last 30 days. |
| `404` | `project not found` | Deleting: the slug is wrong, or you can't see the project. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | Deleting and restoring a project needs the owner tier. Listing deleted projects needs the organization owner or admin role. |

## Related

- [Projects](/docs/platform/projects)
- [Transfer project ownership](/docs/guides/transfer-project-ownership)
- [Review the audit log](/docs/guides/review-the-audit-log)

docs.title: Invite your team
docs.description: Add existing Flagon users to your organization and email invitations to people who don't have an account yet, then track and revoke pending invitations.
headings: List pending invitations (paginated, see the Link header)
docs.body:
Inviting is how people join an organization. Flagon handles two cases with one action: if the
email or username you enter belongs to an existing Flagon user, they are **added right away**;
if it is an email address with no account, Flagon creates a **pending invitation** and emails a
single-use link. That link doubles as email verification, so the invitee registers and joins in
one step.

By the end of this guide your teammates will be members of your organization with the role you
chose, and you will know how to see and revoke invitations that haven't been accepted.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner** or **admin**. You can invite as `member` or `admin` (never
  above your own role). An invitation cannot grant `owner`: an owner promotes someone to owner
  from the member list after they join.
- **API token scope:** `write:org` to invite and revoke, `read:org` to list invitations.

</Callout>

## Organization roles at a glance

| Role | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| `owner` | Full control, including deleting the organization. Only owners can grant or remove the owner role. |
| `admin` | Manages members, invitations, teams, tokens, and settings. Has owner-tier control of every project. |
| `member` | Creates projects. Access to each existing project starts from the organization's [base permission](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions) and can be raised per project. |

See [Roles](/docs/platform/roles) for the full model.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Send the invitations">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open **People** in the sidebar.
2. Select **Invite people**.
3. For each person, enter an **Email or username** and pick a **Role** (Member or Admin).
   Select **Add more** to invite several people at once.
4. Select **Send invites**.

Existing users join immediately and get a notification. Everyone else receives an email, sent
by the Flagon API, with a link to `app.flagon.io/invite/<token>`. If a row fails (for example, the person is already a
member), it stays in the form with the reason so you can fix it and resend just that row. If an
invitation was created but its email was not sent, the dialog shows that invitation's link with a
**Copy** button, so you can deliver it yourself.

Owners can't be invited. To make someone an owner, invite them as a member, then promote them.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/invitations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"login": "dana@example.com", "role": "member"}'
```

`login` is an email address, or the email or username of an existing user. `role` is `admin`,
`member`, or `viewer` and defaults to `member`. The `201` response says which case happened:

```json
{ "status": "added", "user_id": "u_123" }
```

or, for an email with no account:

```json
{
  "status": "invited",
  "email": "dana@example.com",
  "org_name": "Acme Inc",
  "token": "flagon_inv_...",
  "invitation": { "id": "8b2e...", "email": "dana@example.com", "role": "member", "status": "pending", "inviter": null, "expires_at": "...", "created_at": "..." },
  "email_sent": true
}
```

The API emails the invite link itself, the same way for every front door (dashboard, API,
assistant, and MCP). `email_sent` reports whether the email was handed to a mail provider that
delivers; when it is `false` (no provider, the log mailer, or delivery failed), the invitation still exists and you can deliver the link
yourself: `https://app.flagon.io/invite/` followed by the returned `token`. The token is
returned only once and only its hash is stored.

<Callout type="note" title="Self-hosted mail">

On a self-hosted API, invitation email goes out through Resend when `RESEND_API_KEY` is set
(or `FLAGON_MAIL_PROVIDER=resend`). Otherwise the API uses the log mailer, which writes the
email to the server log instead of sending it, and reports `email_sent: false`. See
[Configuration](/docs/reference/configuration).

</Callout>

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

In **Ask AI**, ask:

> Invite dana@example.com to acme as a member.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Invite "dana@example.com" to "acme" as member** and runs it
only after you select **Confirm**. An existing user is added directly. For someone without an
account, the API emails the invite link, and the assistant reports whether the email was sent.
The invite token itself never enters the conversation.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="What the invitee sees">

The link opens a **Join** page showing who invited them, the organization, and the role.

- **Not signed in:** they fill in a name, username, and password. The email field is fixed to
  the invited address and needs no verification code, because the invitation proves they
  control it. Submitting creates the account and joins the organization.
- **Signed in with the invited email:** they select **Join** and land in the organization.
- **Signed in with a different email:** the page explains the mismatch and offers **Sign out**,
  so they can continue with the invited address.

An invitation is valid for **7 days** and can be used once.

</Step>

<Step title="Track and revoke pending invitations">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

On **People**, open the **Pending invitations** tab. Each row shows the email, role, inviter,
and expiry. Select **Revoke** to cancel one; the link stops working immediately.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
# List pending invitations (paginated, see the Link header)
curl https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/invitations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"

# Revoke one by id
curl -X DELETE https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/invitations/8b2e... \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Show me pending invitations in acme.

Then:

> Revoke the invitation for dana@example.com.

The assistant looks up the invitation id with `list_invitations` and proposes
`revoke_invitation` for you to confirm.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

The person appears on the **Members** tab of **People** with the role you chose, and the
organization's [audit log](/docs/guides/review-the-audit-log) records `invitation.sent` and then
`invitation.accepted` (or `member.added` for an existing user who was added directly). You also
get a notification when an invitee accepts.

From the API, `GET /orgs/acme/members` returns `{"members": [...]}` with their `user_id` and
`role`.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `that user is already a member` | Nothing to do; they are already in the organization. |
| `409` | `a pending invitation already exists for that email` | Revoke the existing invitation first if you need to change its role, then invite again. |
| `422` | `enter an email address to invite, or the username of an existing user` | The login is neither an email address nor an existing username. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | You are not an owner or admin, or you tried to grant a role above your own. |
| `422` | `invalid role` (assistant and MCP) or a request validation error (REST) | The role is not `admin`, `member`, or `viewer`. Invitations cannot grant `owner`. |
| `410` | `this invitation has expired` | The invitee used a link older than 7 days. Invite them again. |
| `409` | `this invitation is no longer valid` | The link was already accepted or was revoked. |
| `403` | `this invitation was sent to a different email address` | The invitee accepted while signed in as someone else. They should sign out and use the invited email. |

## Related

- [Members](/docs/platform/members)
- [Roles](/docs/platform/roles)
- [Organize with teams](/docs/guides/organize-with-teams)
- [Set base permissions](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions)

docs.title: Manage project access
docs.description: Give people and teams a role on a specific project, change or revoke it, and work out anyone's effective access.
docs.body:
Every organization member starts each project at the organization's
[base permission](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions). **Project access** is how you go further on
one project: a **collaborator grant** gives one person a role there, and a **team grant** gives
every member of a team a role there. Grants only ever raise access; they never lower someone
below the base permission.

By the end of this guide the right people and teams will hold the right roles on a project, and
you will be able to explain why anyone has the access they have.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** effective **admin** on the project. Organization owners and admins always have it;
  anyone else needs an `admin` grant (direct or through a team) or project ownership. A member
  who created the project was granted `admin` on it automatically.
- **Who can be granted:** only existing organization members. [Invite them](/docs/guides/invite-your-team) first.
- **API token scopes:** `read:project` to list grants, `admin:project` to add, change, or revoke them.

</Callout>

## How effective access works

A person's effective role on a project is the **maximum** of:

1. their organization-derived role: `admin` for organization owners and admins; the base
   permission (default `read`, possibly `none`) for members;
2. their direct collaborator grant on the project, if any;
3. the highest grant held by any team they belong to on the project.

The ladder, lowest to highest, is `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain`, `admin`:

| Needs at least | To |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | See the project at all. Without it, the project returns `404`, as if it did not exist. |
| `write` | Edit the name, description, README, and repository URL. |
| `maintain` | Rename the project's slug (which changes its URL), plus project settings as they are added. |
| `admin` | Manage collaborator and team grants (this guide). |
| owner tier | Delete, restore, and manage owners. See [Transfer project ownership](/docs/guides/transfer-project-ownership). |

The API checks these roles on every project operation, and Postgres row-level security enforces
them again underneath. A project you can see but lack the role for answers `403`.

For example, with a base permission of `read`, Dana has a direct `triage` grant and belongs to
the `platform` team, which holds `write`: her effective role is `write`.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Open the project's access settings">

In the dashboard, open the project, then **Settings > Access**. The page has three sections:
collaborators (direct grants), teams, and owners.

</Step>

<Step title="Add a collaborator">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Select **Add collaborator**, enter the person's email or username, and pick a role. Change a
role from the row's role picker, or revoke it from the same row.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout/members \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"login": "dana@example.com", "role": "write"}'
```

List grants with `GET /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/members` (returns `{"members": [...]}` with
each `user_id`). Change one with
`PUT /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/members/{userId}/role` and `{"role": "maintain"}`; revoke it
with `DELETE /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/members/{userId}`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Give dana@example.com write access to the checkout project.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Grant "dana@example.com" write on project "checkout" in
"acme"**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Add a team">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

In the teams section, select **Add team**, pick the **Team**, and choose a **Role**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"team": "platform", "role": "write"}'
```

Change with `PUT /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams/platform/role`; revoke with
`DELETE /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams/platform`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Give the platform team maintain on checkout.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- The grant appears in the project's **Settings > Access** list.
- The person gets a notification that they were added to the project (or that their role
  changed).
- The audit log records `project.access_granted`, `project.access_changed`,
  `project.access_revoked`, or the `project.team_access_*` equivalents.
- Ask the person to open the project. If they still can't see it, check the base permission and
  whether they are a member of the team you granted.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Things to know

- **You can't change your own access** on a project. Ask another project admin, or an
  organization owner or admin.
- **Revoking a grant never removes base access.** With a base of `read`, a revoked collaborator
  can still see the project. Set the base to `none` for private-by-default projects.
- **Organization owners and admins can't be limited per project.** Their org role already gives
  them `admin` and the owner tier everywhere.
- **Team membership changes take effect immediately.** Remove someone from a team and the access
  that came from that team goes with it.

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `that user must be an organization member first` | Invite them to the organization, then grant access. |
| `409` | `that user already has a role on this project` | Change their role instead of adding them again. |
| `409` | `that team already has a role on this project` | Change the team's role instead. |
| `409` | `you can't change your own access here` | Someone else has to change your grant. |
| `404` | `that user has no role on this project` | There is no direct grant to change or revoke; their access comes from the base permission or a team. |
| `404` | `project not found` | The slug is wrong, or you can't see the project. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | You need effective `admin` on the project. |

## Related

- [Project access](/docs/platform/project-access)
- [Set base permissions](/docs/guides/set-base-permissions)
- [Organize with teams](/docs/guides/organize-with-teams)
- [Transfer project ownership](/docs/guides/transfer-project-ownership)

docs.title: Organize with teams
docs.description: Group organization members into teams, choose who maintains each team, and grant a whole team a role on a project.
docs.body:
A **team** is a named group of organization members, such as `platform` or `payments`. Teams
exist so you can grant access once and have it follow people: give the `platform` team `write`
on a project, and everyone on the team gets `write`; add someone to the team later and they
inherit it automatically. Removing them from the team removes the access that came from it.

By the end of this guide you will have a team with members and a maintainer, and that team will
hold a role on at least one project.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Create or delete a team:** organization **owner** or **admin**.
- **Edit a team or manage its members:** organization owner or admin, or a **maintainer** of
  that team.
- **Grant a team a role on a project:** effective **admin** on that project (organization
  owners and admins always qualify). See [Manage project access](/docs/guides/manage-project-access).
- **API token scopes:** `write:team` to create teams and manage members, `admin:team` to delete
  teams, `admin:project` to grant a team project access.

</Callout>

## Team roles

A team has its own two roles, separate from organization roles and project roles:

| Team role | Can do |
| --- | --- |
| `maintainer` | Edit the team's name, slug, and description, and add, remove, or change the role of its members. |
| `member` | Belongs to the team and receives every project grant the team holds. |

Whoever creates a team becomes its first maintainer, so every team starts with someone who can
manage it. A maintainer cannot delete the team; only organization owners and admins can.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Create the team">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open **Teams** in the sidebar and select **New team**.
2. Enter a **Team name**, and optionally a **Slug** and **Description**.
3. Select **Create team**. Flagon opens the team's page with **Members**, **Projects**, and **Settings** tabs.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/teams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Platform", "description": "Runs shared infrastructure"}'
```

The slug is derived from the name when omitted (`platform`). A `201` returns the team.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Create a team called Platform in acme.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Create team "Platform" in "acme"**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Add members">

Team members must already be members of the organization. [Invite them](/docs/guides/invite-your-team)
first if they aren't.

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

On the team's **Members** tab, add a member by **Email or username** and pick a **Role**
(`maintainer` or `member`). Change a role or remove someone from the same table.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/teams/platform/members \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"login": "dana@example.com", "role": "member"}'
```

`role` is required. Change it later with
`PUT /orgs/acme/teams/platform/members/{userId}/role` and a body of `{"role": "maintainer"}`,
or remove the person with `DELETE /orgs/acme/teams/platform/members/{userId}`. Get `userId`
from `GET /orgs/acme/teams/platform/members`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Add dana@example.com to the platform team as a maintainer.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Give the team a project role">

A team grant uses the project role ladder: `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain`, `admin`.

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Either open the project and go to **Settings > Access**, then **Add team** in the teams section;
or open the team's **Projects** tab and add a project there. Choose the **Team** (or
**Project**) and a **Role**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"team": "platform", "role": "write"}'
```

Change the role with `PUT /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams/platform/role`, or revoke it with
`DELETE /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams/platform`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Give the platform team write access to the checkout project.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Grant team "platform" write on project "checkout" in
"acme"**.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- The team's **Projects** tab lists the project and the role.
- `GET /orgs/acme/teams/platform/projects` returns `{"projects": [...]}` with the granted role.
- `GET /orgs/acme/projects/checkout/teams` returns the team in `{"teams": [...]}`.
- The audit log records `team.created`, `team.member_added`, and
  `project.team_access_granted`.

A member's access to the project is now at least the team's role. If they also have an
organization base permission or a direct grant, the highest one wins.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Deleting a team

Deleting a team (organization owners and admins, `admin:team`) frees its slug and removes every
project grant and project ownership the team held, so members lose any access that came only
from the team. From the dashboard use the team's **Settings** tab; from the API,
`DELETE /orgs/acme/teams/platform`.

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `a team with that slug already exists` | Choose another name or slug. |
| `409` | `that user must be an organization member first` | Invite the person to the organization, then add them to the team. |
| `409` | `that user is already on this team` | Change their role instead. |
| `409` | `that team already has a role on this project` | Change the team's role instead of adding it again. |
| `404` | `team not found` | Check the team slug. Deleted teams are not found. |
| `404` | `no user with that email or username` | Check the login; the person needs a Flagon account and organization membership. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | You are not an owner, admin, or maintainer of this team, or not an admin on the project. |

## Related

- [Teams](/docs/platform/teams)
- [Manage project access](/docs/guides/manage-project-access)
- [Project access](/docs/platform/project-access)
- [Invite your team](/docs/guides/invite-your-team)

docs.title: Require two-factor authentication
docs.description: Turn on the organization-wide two-factor requirement, and understand what happens to members who haven't set it up.
docs.body:
**Two-factor authentication (2FA)** adds a second step at sign-in, a 6-digit code from an
authenticator app, so a stolen password alone can't open an account. Each person turns on 2FA
for their own account. An organization can then **require** it: members without 2FA can't use
the organization, from the dashboard, the API, or the assistant, until they enable it.

By the end of this guide your organization will require 2FA, and you will know what members
without it experience and how to check who is affected.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner** or **admin**.
- **Your own 2FA:** enabled on your account first. Flagon won't let you turn the requirement on
  otherwise (the dashboard disables the switch and the API answers `403`), so you can't lock
  yourself out.
- **API token scopes:** `read:org` to read the policy, `write:org` to change it.

</Callout>

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Enable 2FA on your own account">

Go to your personal **Settings > Password and authentication** (`/settings/security`), and
under **Two-factor authentication** enable **Authenticator app (TOTP)**. Confirm your password,
scan the QR code with an authenticator app, enter a code, and save your backup codes somewhere
safe.

</Step>

<Step title="Turn on the requirement">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open organization **Settings > Authentication** (under **Security**).
2. Turn on **Require two-factor authentication**.

If the switch is disabled with a warning to enable 2FA on your own account first, finish the
previous step. Turning the requirement off is always allowed.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

The requirement is `enforce_two_factor` in the organization's security policy. `PUT` replaces
the whole policy, so read it first and send every field back:

```bash
curl https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/security \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
# {"enforce_two_factor": false, "require_sso": false, "base_permission": "read"}

curl -X PUT https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/security \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enforce_two_factor": true, "require_sso": false, "base_permission": "read"}'
```

The API enforces the lockout check itself: if your own account has no 2FA, turning the
requirement on returns `403` with
`enable two-factor authentication on your own account before requiring it for the organization`.
The check applies only when the requirement goes from off to on, and never to organization
access tokens.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Require two-factor authentication for everyone in acme.

The assistant proposes **Confirm: Update security policy for "acme"** and changes only
`enforce_two_factor`.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="What members without 2FA see">

The next time a member without 2FA opens any page in the organization, Flagon redirects them to
a **Two-factor authentication required** page that names the organization. It offers:

- **Set up two-factor**, which opens their personal security settings (outside the organization,
  so the redirect can't loop);
- **I've enabled it - continue**, which takes them back into the organization.

They stay members, keep their roles, and can still use their personal settings and any other
organizations that don't require 2FA. Nothing is deleted; they just can't use this organization
until 2FA is on. Leaving the organization is still allowed.

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- `GET /orgs/acme/security` returns `"enforce_two_factor": true`, and every organization object
  (for example in `GET /orgs`) carries the same flag.
- The audit log records `organization.security_changed` with the summary
  `enabled the two-factor authentication requirement`.
- Sign in as a test member without 2FA and open the organization: you land on the
  **Two-factor authentication required** page.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Where the requirement applies

The API enforces the requirement, not just the dashboard. It checks every operation under
`/orgs/<slug>/...` (except leaving the organization), every assistant and MCP tool call that
names the organization, and every assistant conversation in it. A member without 2FA gets
`403` with
`this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue`,
whether they call from a dashboard session or with a **personal access token**. The dashboard
adds the redirect to the **Two-factor authentication required** page on top.

<Callout type="note" title="Organization access tokens are exempt">

An organization access token acts as a service identity that never signs in interactively, so
the 2FA requirement does not apply to it. Owners and admins control those tokens' lifetimes and
scopes; review and revoke them as part of your policy. See
[Automate with access tokens](/docs/guides/automate-with-access-tokens).

</Callout>

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | Only owners and admins can read or change the policy. |
| `403` | `enable two-factor authentication on your own account before requiring it for the organization` | Turn on 2FA for your own account, then try again. |
| `403` | `this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue` | The caller has no 2FA. Enable it in personal **Settings > Password and authentication**. |
| `422` | `validation failed` | The `PUT` body is missing a field. Send `enforce_two_factor`, `require_sso`, and `base_permission` together. |

## Related

- [Two-factor authentication](/docs/platform/two-factor)
- [Set up SSO with OIDC](/docs/guides/set-up-sso-oidc)
- [Review the audit log](/docs/guides/review-the-audit-log)
- [Account](/docs/platform/account)

docs.title: Review the audit log
docs.description: Find out who changed what in your organization, filter and page through events, and decide whether actor IP addresses are shown.
docs.body:
The **audit log** is an append-only record of every change to your organization's state:
projects created and deleted, members added and removed, roles and grants changed, tokens
created and revoked, security settings and SSO providers changed. Each entry is written in the
same database transaction as the change it describes, so a change without its audit entry can't
happen. Entries can't be edited or deleted.

By the end of this guide you will be able to answer "who did what, where, and when" for your
organization from the dashboard, the API, or the assistant, and control whether IP addresses
are visible.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner** or **admin**. Members can't read the audit log.
- **API token scopes:** `read:org` to read the log and its settings, `write:org` to change
  IP disclosure.

</Callout>

## What an event contains

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | A stable key such as `project.deleted` or `member.role_changed`. |
| `summary` | A human sentence, for example `deleted project Checkout Service`. |
| `actor_id`, `actor_name`, `actor_email`, `actor_username` | Who did it. |
| `target_type`, `target_id` | What it was done to, for example `project` and the project slug. |
| `actor_country`, `actor_user_agent` | Where the request came from. |
| `actor_ip` | The client IP address. Always recorded; returned only when IP disclosure is on, otherwise `null`. |
| `created_at` | When it happened. |

The [Audit actions reference](/docs/reference/audit-actions) lists every action key.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Open the log">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Open organization **Settings > Audit log** (under **Logs**). The **Events** tab lists entries
newest first. Expand a row to see every field, including the event id and client. Select
**Load more** at the bottom for older entries.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -i https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/audit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
```

The body is `{"events": [...]}`. When there are more, the response carries a `Link` header
with `rel="next"`; follow that URL to get the next page. `limit` sets the page size (default
30, maximum 100).

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> What changed in acme this week?

The assistant reads recent entries with `list_audit_events` and summarizes them. Reading never
needs confirmation.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Search and filter">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

Type in **Search audit logs...** to match summaries, actions, actors, and locations. Use
**Filter by action** to pick one or more actions, and **Clear filters** to reset.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

| Query parameter | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `q` | Free-text search across summary, action, actor, and location (and the IP address, only while IP disclosure is on). |
| `action` | Only these action keys. Repeat it for several. |
| `actor` | Only events by this user id. |
| `limit` | Page size, 1 to 100. |
| `cursor` | The opaque cursor from a previous `Link` header. |

```bash
curl -G https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/audit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "action=project.deleted" \
  --data-urlencode "action=project.restored" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=50"
```

The `Link` header keeps your filters, so following it pages through the same filtered view.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Who deleted projects in acme recently?

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Decide on IP disclosure">

IP addresses are always recorded. **IP disclosure** only controls whether owners and admins can
see them in the log. It is off by default. Because it exposes members' IP addresses, review it
with whoever handles privacy in your organization before turning it on.

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

On **Settings > Audit log**, open the **Settings** tab, check **Enable source IP disclosure**,
and select **Save**.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/audit/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ip_disclosure": true}'
```

Read the current value with `GET /orgs/acme/audit/config`.

</Tab>

<Tab title="Assistant">

> Turn on IP disclosure for the acme audit log.

The assistant proposes the change for you to confirm.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

</Step>

<Step title="Verify it worked">

- Changing IP disclosure is itself audited as `organization.audit_config_changed`.
- With disclosure on, `actor_ip` is filled in on events (including past ones, since the IP was
  always recorded). With it off, `actor_ip` is `null`.

</Step>

</Steps>

## Things to know

- **Requests through a token are audited too.** An organization access token acts as its own
  service principal, so its changes show that token's name as the actor. A personal access
  token's changes show you.
- **Where comes from the request.** For dashboard actions, including changes you confirm in
  the assistant, Flagon records the end user's IP, country, and browser, which the dashboard
  forwards; the API trusts those forwarded values only from the dashboard itself. For direct API
  and MCP calls with a token it records the calling client's own IP (on the hosted service, from
  the `Fly-Client-IP` header; self-hosted, the header named by `FLAGON_CLIENT_IP_HEADER`, or else
  the connection's address) and its `User-Agent`, so give your scripts a descriptive
  `User-Agent`.
- **The audit log is not notifications.** Notifications tell a person about something that
  affects them; the audit log is the organization's record for admins.

## Common failures

| Status | `detail` | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `403` | `only organization owners and admins can do that` | You are a member. Only owners and admins can read the log. |
| `404` | `organization not found` | The slug is wrong, or you are not a member of the organization. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | Reading or changing IP disclosure needs owner or admin. |
| `422` | `invalid pagination cursor` | Use the cursor from the latest `Link` header unchanged. |

## Related

- [Audit log](/docs/platform/audit-log)
- [Audit actions reference](/docs/reference/audit-actions)
- [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination)
- [Notifications](/docs/platform/notifications)

docs.title: Set base permissions
docs.description: Choose the default project access every organization member gets, and understand how it combines with direct and team grants.
docs.body:
The **base permission** is the project role every organization member gets on every project in
the organization, without anyone granting it project by project. It is a floor, not a ceiling:
a direct grant or a team grant can raise a member above it on a specific project, but nothing
lowers a member below it. New organizations start at `read`, so members can see every project
until you decide otherwise.

By the end of this guide your organization's base permission will match how open you want
projects to be, and you will know how to check what a given member can actually do.

<Callout type="info" title="Before you start">

- **Role:** organization **owner** or **admin**.
- **API token scopes:** `read:org` to read the setting, `write:org` to change it.

</Callout>

## How effective access is computed

A person's effective role on a project is the **highest** of three sources:

| Source | What it grants |
| --- | --- |
| Organization role | Owners and admins get `admin` on every project, plus the owner tier (delete, restore, manage owners). Members get the base permission. |
| Direct project grant | A role given to that person on that project. |
| Team grants | The highest role held by any team the person belongs to on that project. |

The project role ladder, lowest to highest, is `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain`, `admin`.
What each level lets you do on a project:

| Effective role | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| none | Nothing. The project is invisible: requests for it return `404`. |
| `read` | View the project, its README, collaborators, teams, and owners. |
| `write` | Edit the project's name, description, README, and repository URL. |
| `maintain` | Rename the project's slug (which changes its URL), plus project settings as they are added. |
| `admin` | Grant, change, and revoke collaborator and team access. |

A project you can see but lack the role for answers `403`. `triage` sits between `read` and
`write` and currently grants the same as `read`. The API checks these roles on every project
operation, and Postgres row-level security enforces them again underneath. Deleting,
restoring, and managing owners need the owner tier above `admin`; see
[Transfer project ownership](/docs/guides/transfer-project-ownership).

## Choose a level

| Base permission | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | Projects are private by default. Members see only projects they, or a team they're on, have been granted. |
| `read` (default) | Everyone can see everything; changes need an explicit grant. |
| `write` | Small, high-trust organizations where every member edits every project. |
| `admin` | Every member can manage access on every project. Rarely what you want. |

The dashboard offers these four. The API and assistant also accept `triage` and `maintain`.

## Steps

<Steps>

<Step title="Change the base permission">

<Tabs>

<Tab title="Dashboard">

1. Open **Settings** in the sidebar, then **Member privileges** (under **Access**).
2. In **Base permission**, pick **No access**, **Read**, **Write**, or **Admin**.

The change saves as soon as you pick a value. If it fails, the selection reverts and an error
appears under the card.

</Tab>

<Tab title="API">

The base permission lives in the organization's security policy, alongside the 2FA and SSO
requirements. `PUT` replaces the whole policy, so read it first and send all three fields back:

```bash
curl https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/security \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN"
# {"enforce_two_factor": false, "require_sso": false, "base_permission": "read"}

curl -X PUT https://api.flagon.io/orgs/acme/security \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGON_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
```
