docs.title: Access and permissions
docs.description: Why an organization or project shows 404 instead of 403, how to tell a token scope problem from a role or organization policy problem, base permission surprises, and what happens to deleted organizations and projects.
headings: 403: is it the token or the role?
You can't see the audit log
docs.body:
Access in Flagon is decided by independent checks. Your **role** (in the
organization, and on each project) decides what you may do. When you use an
access token, its **scopes** decide which operations that token may call, and it
can never do more than your role allows. On top of both, an organization can
require **two-factor authentication** or **single sign-on**, and the API refuses
requests from members who do not meet that policy. Most "why can't I" questions
come down to which check said no, and the status code and message tell you
which.

## An organization returns 404, not 403

<Callout type="warn" title="The organization page or API says it doesn't exist">

Opening `/<org>` shows a 404 page, or the API answers `404 Not Found` with
`organization not found`, but you know the organization is real.

</Callout>

**What it means.** Flagon answers the same way for an organization that does not
exist, one you are not a member of, and one that was deleted. It never confirms
that an organization exists outside your reach, so a 404 is the expected answer
where you might expect a 403. The dashboard's 404 page is also deliberately
generic for the same reason. Projects and teams inside an organization you can't
see return 404 as well.

The same applies to projects inside an organization you do belong to. If your
effective role on a project is below `read` (for example the organization's base
permission is `none` and nobody granted you access), the project returns `404`
"project not found", for reads and for changes alike, and it is left out of the
project list. Ask a project admin or an organization owner or admin for a grant.

**How to fix.**

1. Check the slug in the URL or request. Slugs are lowercase.
2. Make sure you are signed in as the account that belongs to the organization.
   The organization switcher lists every organization your account is in.
3. Ask an owner or admin to [invite you](/docs/guides/invite-your-team).
4. If the organization was deleted, see [deleted organizations](#deleted-organizations-and-projects).
5. Using an **organization access token**? It acts only inside the organization
   that issued it, so every other organization returns 404. Use a personal access
   token, or a token issued by the other organization.

## 403: is it the token or the role?

A `403 Forbidden` always means Flagon knows who you are and has decided you may
not do this. The message says which check refused:

| Message | Which check | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` | The token's **scopes** | Create a token that includes the scope the operation needs, then revoke the old one. Scopes are fixed when a token is created. |
| `you don't have permission to do that` | Your **role** (or, for an organization token, the token's role) | Ask an owner or admin for a higher role or a project grant. A token cannot fix this: it never exceeds its principal's permissions. |
| `only an organization owner can delete it` / `only an organization owner can restore it` | Your organization **role** | Only owners delete or restore an organization. |
| `only organization owners and admins can do that` | Your organization **role** | The audit log (and other admin-only reads) needs an owner or admin. |
| `this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue` | The organization's **2FA requirement** | Enable two-factor authentication on your account at `/settings/security`. Tokens you already hold start working again once it is on. |
| `this organization requires single sign-on; sign in through the organization's identity provider to continue` | The organization's **SSO requirement**, for a dashboard session | Sign out and sign in again through the organization's identity provider (**Continue with SSO**). |
| `this organization requires single sign-on; sign in through the organization's identity provider at least once before using a personal access token with it` | The **SSO requirement**, for a personal access token | Sign in to the dashboard through the organization's identity provider once. The token then works. Alternatively, use an organization access token, which the policy does not apply to. |
| `this operation requires a user; organization access tokens can't perform it` | The **kind of token** | Creating, leaving, listing deleted, or restoring organizations need a person. Use a personal access token or the dashboard. |

The organization policy checks apply to every `/orgs/{slug}/...` operation
except leaving the organization, to assistant and MCP tools that name the
organization, and to the assistant itself. Organization owners are exempt from
the SSO requirement, so an owner can always reach settings to fix a broken
provider. Organization access tokens are exempt from both requirements.

Every operation's scope is listed in the [scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes).
A parent scope implies its children, so `admin:org` covers `write:org` and
`read:org`. Over MCP, the same scope failure reads
`this token is missing the scope required for <tool name>`.

## Base permission surprises

The **base permission** (Settings, then Access, then Member privileges) is the
project role every organization **member** gets on every project. The dashboard
offers `none`, `read`, `write`, and `admin`, and owners or admins change it. A few
consequences catch people out:

- **It is a floor, not a ceiling.** A project grant (to a person or a team) can
  raise a member above the base permission on one project, but nothing lowers a
  member below it. To keep one project private from most members, lower the base
  permission for everyone and grant access where it's needed.
- **Owners and admins are unaffected.** Organization owners and admins are
  project admins everywhere and hold owner authority on every project, whatever
  the base permission says.
- **`admin` is broad.** Setting the base permission to `admin` makes every member
  an admin on every project, so every member can manage every project's
  collaborators and team grants.
- **Each project action has its own minimum.** Viewing a project needs `read`,
  editing its name, description, README, or repository URL needs `write`,
  changing its slug needs `maintain`, and managing collaborators and team grants
  needs `admin`. A member who can view a project but lacks the role for an action
  gets `403` with `you don't have permission to do that`.
- **Deleting a project needs ownership, not admin.** Deleting, restoring, and
  changing a project's owners are owner-tier actions: a project owner (a person or
  a team) or an organization owner or admin. A project admin who is not an owner
  gets `403` with `you don't have permission to do that`.
- **Creating a project does not make you its owner.** The creator is granted
  `admin` on the new project, which lets them manage its access but not delete
  it.
- **The change applies to everyone at once.** Lowering it takes access away from
  every member who has no explicit grant, immediately.

See [Roles and permissions](/docs/platform/roles) for the full model.

## You can't see the audit log

The audit log is readable by organization **owners and admins** only. Anyone
else gets `403` "only organization owners and admins can do that", from the REST
API and from the `list_audit_events` tool the assistant and MCP use.

## Deleted organizations and projects

**A deleted organization** disappears for everyone at once: its pages and API
operations return `404`, its organization access tokens stop working (`401`),
and its slug is freed. Owners can restore it for 30 days from **Settings, then
Organizations, then Recently deleted** in personal settings (or
`POST /deleted-orgs/{id}/restore`). Restore can fail with:

| Status | Message | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `that org slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Pass a new `slug` in the restore request body. |
| `402` | `the free plan includes one organization; add a payment method to restore another` | You already own as many organizations as the plan allows. |
| `404` | `no restorable organization with that id` | The 30 days have passed, or you were not an owner. |

**A deleted project** returns `404` with `project not found`, and its slug is
free for a new project immediately. Project owners, and organization owners and
admins, restore it for 30 days from the organization's **Settings, then Archive,
then Deleted projects** (or `POST /orgs/{slug}/projects/{project}/restore`).
Restore can fail with:

| Status | Message | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409` | `that project slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Pass a new `slug` in the restore request body, or rename the project that took it. |
| `404` | `no restorable project with that slug` | The 30 days have passed, or the project is not deleted. |
| `403` | `you don't have permission to do that` | Restoring needs project ownership, or organization owner or admin. |

See [Delete and restore](/docs/guides/delete-and-restore).

## Related

- [Roles and permissions](/docs/platform/roles)
- [Project access](/docs/platform/project-access)
- [Scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes)
- [API errors](/docs/troubleshooting/api-errors)

docs.title: API errors
docs.description: Every error status the Flagon API returns, the real messages behind each one, what causes them, and how to fix them.
docs.body:
Every Flagon API error is a problem-details object with a `status` and a
`detail` message (see [Errors](/docs/api/errors) for the shape). This page is the
other half: for each status, the messages you will actually see, what causes
them, and what to change. The same condition produces the same status whether
you call the REST API, confirm an assistant action, or call a tool over MCP.

Branch your code on the **status**. Use the **message** to understand a specific
failure; wording can improve over time. Every response, success or failure,
carries an `X-Request-Id` header; keep it when you log a failure, because it is
how a failure is found in the API's log.

## 400 Bad Request

The request could not be read at all: the body is not valid JSON, or a required
body is missing. Check that you send `Content-Type: application/json` and a
well-formed body.

Confirming an assistant action with a tool that does not exist, or one that is
not a confirmable change, returns `400` with
`unknown or non-executable tool: <name>`.

## 401 Unauthorized

Flagon could not establish who you are.

| Message | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid or expired token` | The `flagon_` access token is unknown, revoked, or past its expiry, or it is an organization token whose organization was deleted. | Create a new token. Check for stray whitespace or a truncated value in your secret store. |
| `invalid internal token` | A request without a `flagon_` token was checked against the app's internal token and did not match. From your own code, this almost always means the token is missing or does not start with `flagon_`. | Send `Authorization: Bearer flagon_...`. On a self-hosted instance where the **app** gets this, the app's and API's `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN` differ. |
| `missing user identity` | The internal token was valid but no user was named. Only the app uses the internal path. | Self-hosted: make sure requests to the API go through the app's gateway, not directly with the internal token. |

## 402 Payment Required

`the free plan includes one organization; add a payment method to create more`

You already own an organization, and the free plan includes one. Restoring a
deleted organization counts too, and fails with
`the free plan includes one organization; add a payment method to restore another`.
Organizations you are a member of but do not own do not count, and neither do
deleted ones. Delete or transfer ownership of an organization you own, or ask
someone else to create the new one and invite you.

<Callout type="warn" title="Not available yet">

Paid plans and payment methods are not built yet, so there is currently no way
to raise this limit on the hosted service.

</Callout>

## 403 Forbidden

You are authenticated but not allowed. Several checks produce it:

- `this token is missing the scope required for this operation` means your
  **token** lacks the operation's scope. Create a token with that scope. See the
  [scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes).
- `you don't have permission to do that` means your **role** does not allow the
  action. Ask an owner or admin for more access.
- `this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue`
  means the organization requires 2FA and your account does not have it. Enable
  it, and the same token works again.
- `this organization requires single sign-on; sign in through the organization's identity provider to continue`
  (dashboard sessions) or
  `this organization requires single sign-on; sign in through the organization's identity provider at least once before using a personal access token with it`
  (personal access tokens) means the organization requires SSO. Sign in through
  its identity provider.
- `this operation requires a user; organization access tokens can't perform it`
  means an organization access token called an operation that needs a person:
  creating, leaving, listing deleted, or restoring organizations, or mirroring a
  profile.

Other `403` messages name the rule directly, for example
`only an organization owner can delete it`,
`only organization owners and admins can do that` (the audit log), or
`this invitation was sent to a different email address` (sign in as the invited
address to accept). [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions#403-is-it-the-token-or-the-role)
covers how to tell the two apart.

## 404 Not Found

The resource does not exist, or you can't see it. Flagon does not distinguish
the two, so it never confirms something exists outside your reach.

| Message | Common causes |
| --- | --- |
| `organization not found` | Wrong slug, you are not a member, the organization was deleted, or you are using another organization's access token. |
| `project not found` | Wrong project slug, the project was deleted, or your effective role on it is below `read`. |
| `team not found` | Wrong team slug. |
| `invitation not found` | The invitation was revoked or already used. |
| `that user is not a member` | Managing a member who isn't in the organization. |
| `that user has no role on this project` / `that team has no role on this project` | Removing a project grant that doesn't exist. |
| `no restorable organization with that id` | The organization's 30-day restore window passed, or you were not an owner. |
| `no restorable project with that slug` | The project's 30-day restore window passed, or it is not deleted. |

See [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions#an-organization-returns-404-not-403).

## 409 Conflict

The request is valid but conflicts with the current state.

| Message | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `that org slug is already taken` | Choose another slug. Slugs are unique across the whole instance, and a deleted organization frees its slug. |
| `a project with that slug already exists` | Choose another slug. |
| `that project slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Pass a new `slug` in the restore body, or rename the project that took the slug. |
| `a team with that slug already exists` | Choose another team slug. |
| `that username is already taken` | Choose another username. |
| `that org slug is now taken; restore it under a new slug` | Pass a new `slug` in the restore body. |
| `that user is already a member` | Nothing to do, or change their role instead. |
| `a pending invitation already exists for that email` | Resend or revoke the existing invitation. |
| `this invitation is no longer valid` | It was accepted or revoked; ask for a new one. |
| `an organization must always have an owner` | Promote another member to owner before demoting or removing the last one. |
| `you're the only owner; transfer ownership or delete the organization first` | The sole owner can't leave; promote someone or delete the organization. |
| `you can't change your own membership here; use Leave instead` | Use **Leave** to remove yourself. |
| `that user must be an organization member first` | Invite the person to the organization before granting project access. |
| `that user already has a role on this project` / `that team already has a role on this project` | Change the existing grant instead of adding one. |

## 410 Gone

`this invitation has expired`. Invitations are valid for seven days. Ask an
owner or admin to send a new one.

## 413 Request Entity Too Large

The request body is over a size limit. Two limits apply:

| Message | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `request body is too large limit=1048576 bytes` | The per-operation limit on REST operations, 1 MiB. |
| `request body is too large` | The API-wide cap on every route, including MCP: `FLAGON_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, 4 MiB by default. |

Send less data per request, for example a shorter README or fewer items at once.

## 422 Unprocessable Entity

The request was readable but not valid. Two kinds:

**Schema validation.** `detail` is `validation failed`, and the `errors` list
names each problem with its `location` (such as `body.name`) and `value`:

```json
{
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "validation failed",
  "errors": [
    { "message": "expected required property name to be present", "location": "body", "value": {} }
  ]
}
```

**Domain rules.** A single message says what is wrong. Common ones:

| Message | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `name is required` | Send a non-empty `name`. |
| `slug must contain a letter or digit` | Slugs are normalized to lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; send one with at least one letter or digit. |
| `invalid role` | Use a role from the [roles matrix](/docs/reference/roles-matrix). |
| `invalid base permission` | Use `none`, `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain`, or `admin`. |
| `a name is required` | Tokens need a name. |
| `select at least one scope, or choose full access` | Pass `scopes`, or `full: true`. |
| `unknown scope: <scope>` | Check the spelling against the [scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes). |
| `expiration must be in the future` | Pick a later expiry. |
| `invalid pagination cursor` | Pass the cursor from the previous page's `Link: rel="next"` header unchanged, and use it only with the same list and filters. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination). |
| `enter an email address to invite, or the username of an existing user` | The invitee must be an email or a registered username. |

## 429 Too Many Requests

Two different limits return `429`.

**`rate limit exceeded; retry after <n>s`** comes from the API's request rate
limiter. Each principal (a signed-in user, an access token, or an anonymous
client IP) may make 50 requests per second sustained, with bursts of up to 300,
by default. The response carries a `Retry-After` header with the number of
seconds to wait. Back off for at least that long, and spread bulk work out rather
than firing requests in parallel. Each access token has its own budget, counted
separately on each API machine. On a self-hosted instance the limits are
`FLAGON_RATE_LIMIT` and `FLAGON_RATE_BURST`; `/healthz` and `/readyz` are never
limited.

**`AI usage limit reached for this organization`** means the organization used
its daily allowance of assistant calls (100 per rolling 24 hours by default),
counting both turns and confirmed actions. Only the assistant is limited: the
dashboard, REST API, and MCP keep working. Capacity returns gradually as older
calls age out of the window. See [Usage and AI limits](/docs/platform/usage).

Sign-in pages have their own rate limits, which also return `429`; see
[Sign-in and SSO](/docs/troubleshooting/sign-in-and-sso#too-many-requests-please-try-again-later).

## 500 Internal Server Error

Something failed that Flagon did not expect. The `detail` is a generic line for
the operation, such as `could not create token` or `agent error`. The underlying
cause is never included in the response: the API logs it together with the
request id. Retry; if it keeps happening, report it with the time, the request,
the response body, and the `X-Request-Id` response header (see
[Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/overview#still-stuck)). On a self-hosted
instance, search the API's log for that id. An `agent error` usually means the AI
provider call failed; see
[Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp).

## 503 Service Unavailable

A dependency the request needs is not available right now.

| Message | Where | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `The Flagon API is unreachable right now. Try again shortly.` | The dashboard | The app could not connect to the API at all. Usually brief. Self-hosted: see [the app can't reach the API](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues#the-app-cant-reach-the-api). |
| `AI usage could not be recorded; please try again` | The assistant | The turn ran but its usage could not be saved, so Flagon failed it rather than leave it unmetered. Retry. |
| `the AI agent is not configured` | The assistant | The API has no usable model: the provider key is missing, or the provider rejected it (`401` or `403` upstream). Self-hosted: check `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `FLAGON_AI_API_KEY`. See [Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp). |
| `Single sign-on is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.` | SSO sign-in | The app could not load the SSO provider from the API. Retry; self-hosted, check the app-to-API connection. |
| `identity API is not configured` | Self-hosted API | The API has no internal token, so it rejects the app's calls. A current API refuses to start in production without `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, so this points at an embedded or custom build. Set the token on both sides. |

## Related

- [Errors](/docs/api/errors)
- [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions)
- [Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp)
- [Scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes)

docs.title: Assistant and MCP
docs.description: Fixes for the in-product assistant (usage limits, mock mode, provider errors, organization scope, confirmations) and for MCP clients (authentication, missing tools, scope errors, rate limits, transport).

docs.body:
The in-product assistant and the MCP server are two front doors to the same tool
registry the REST API is built on. The **assistant** runs a model on Flagon's
side, reads freely, and proposes changes for you to confirm. **MCP** lets an
external agent (such as Claude Desktop or Cursor) call the same tools with a
Flagon access token. Problems usually come from one of three places: the
organization's AI allowance, the model configuration, or the credential an MCP
client presents.

## The assistant

### "AI usage limit reached for this organization"

The assistant returned `429 Too Many Requests`. Each organization has a daily
allowance of AI calls over a rolling 24 hours (100 by default). Every message you
send counts as one call, and so does every change you confirm. The allowance
belongs to the organization, so other members' use counts too. The limit is
checked before a confirmed change runs as well, so at the limit, **Confirm** fails
with the same `429` and nothing changes.

Wait for older calls to age out of the window; there is no midnight reset.
Everything else, including the dashboard, the REST API, and MCP, keeps working
in the meantime. On your own instance, raise the limit with
`FLAGON_AI_DAILY_LIMIT` (`0` removes it). See [Usage and AI limits](/docs/platform/usage).

### The assistant answers in "mock mode"

The reply begins "I'm Flagon's local assistant running in offline **mock**
mode - no AI model is configured, so I match on keywords instead of reasoning."

**What it means.** The API has no model configured and fell back to the offline
mock provider. The mock understands a few phrases (list, create, who am I) and
nothing else. This only happens on self-hosted instances.

**How to fix.** Configure a provider on the API and restart it: set
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or point `FLAGON_AI_BASE_URL` at any OpenAI-compatible
endpoint (a local Ollama server is `http://localhost:11434/v1`). The API logs
which provider it chose at boot (`AI agent enabled`, with `provider` and
`model`). See [Configuration](/docs/self-hosting/configuration#ai).

### "the AI agent is not configured"

The assistant returned `503`. The API has no usable model: there is no provider
key, or the provider rejected the key it has (a `401` or `403` from the
provider). Set or replace `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or `FLAGON_AI_API_KEY` for an
OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and restart the API.

Pinning a provider without its key no longer gets this far: with
`FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic` and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, the API refuses to
start with `FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or --anthropic-api-key); unset FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER to fall back automatically`,
and an unknown provider name fails the same way. See
[Self-hosting issues](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues).

### "agent error"

The assistant returned `500` with `agent error`. The call to the model failed for
another reason: the model name is wrong, the endpoint is down, or the provider
returned an error. The response does not include the provider's message; on your
own instance, find it in the API's log under the response's `X-Request-Id`. Fix
the provider settings and restart the API.

### "AI usage could not be recorded; please try again"

The assistant returned `503`. The turn ran, but Flagon could not record its usage
against the organization, so it failed the turn rather than let it go unmetered.
Retry. If it persists on your own instance, check `/readyz`: this usually means
the database is unavailable.

### The assistant says it can't do something

The assistant is confined to operating Flagon. It declines unrelated requests,
and it can only do what a tool in the registry can do. If you ask for something
that isn't built (deployments or logs, for example), it has no tool for it.
It also acts **as you**: anything your role or the organization's settings
forbid, it cannot do either, and it reports the same `403` or `404` you would get.
That includes the organization's security policy: if the organization requires
two-factor authentication or SSO and you do not meet it, the assistant answers
`403` with the same message as the REST API (see
[Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions)).

A conversation is confined to the organization you opened it in. Asking it to act
in another organization fails with a message such as
`this conversation is scoped to the "acme" organization and can't act in "other"; switch to that organization in Flagon to work there`.
Switch organizations in the dashboard and ask there. Restoring a deleted
organization is refused from the assistant with a message ending
`use the Flagon dashboard for it`; use **Recently deleted** in your personal
settings instead.

### The assistant can't find internal pages

No page is marked `internal` today; the handbook is public. When a page is
internal, the assistant can read it, and so can an MCP client that presents a
valid access token. The public `/docs` routes and an anonymous MCP client never
see it, so if an MCP client can't find an internal page, check that it sends
`Authorization: Bearer flagon_...`.

Each message runs at most six rounds of tool calls. For a large request, ask in
smaller steps.

### Why a change needs your confirmation

Reading runs immediately. Anything that **changes** data (creating a project,
inviting a member, changing a setting) comes back as a **proposed action** with
a one-line summary, and nothing happens until you choose **Confirm**. This keeps
you in control of every write the model suggests, even when the model misreads
your intent.

When you confirm, the action runs through the same permission-checked operation
as the dashboard and the REST API. If it fails, you get that operation's real
error (`403`, `404`, `409`, or `422`), not a generic one. The action runs with
exactly the input the assistant proposed, so read the summary before you
confirm.

## MCP clients

### The client only sees `search_docs` and `get_doc`

The client is connecting **anonymously**. Without a Flagon token, the MCP
endpoint exposes only the public documentation tools. Add the header
`Authorization: Bearer flagon_...` with a personal or organization access token
in your client's MCP server settings. `tools/list` then returns every tool your
token's scopes allow. See [Connect an MCP client](/docs/guides/connect-an-mcp-client).

A bearer value that does not start with `flagon_` is treated as no token at all.

### "invalid or expired token" (code -32001)

A `flagon_` token was presented but did not resolve: it was revoked, it expired,
or its organization was deleted. Flagon rejects the request rather than quietly
treating you as anonymous, so a rotated token is obvious. Create a new token and
update the client.

If you instead get an HTTP `503` with "the service is temporarily unavailable",
Flagon couldn't check the token (for example, its database is down). The token
may be fine: retry later and quote the `X-Request-Id` header if you report it.

### "unknown tool: ..." (code -32602)

The tool name does not exist, or it exists but requires authentication and you
connected anonymously. Anonymous callers are never told that authenticated tools
exist. Check the name against `tools/list` after authenticating.

### "this token is missing the scope required for ..." (code -32003)

You are authenticated, but the token does not hold the tool's scope. Tools carry
the same scope as the REST operation they front, so the
[scopes reference](/docs/reference/scopes) applies. Create a token with the
scope and revoke the old one.

### A tool call returns `isError: true`

The tool ran and the operation refused, for example because of a permission check,
the organization's two-factor or SSO requirement, or a slug conflict. The text is
the same safe message the REST API would return (such as `project not found` or
`this organization requires two-factor authentication; enable it on your account to continue`).
An unexpected internal failure reads `something went wrong; please try again`.

### HTTP `429` or `413` instead of a JSON-RPC response

These come from the API in front of the MCP endpoint, so they are plain HTTP
problem responses, not JSON-RPC errors. `429` with
`rate limit exceeded; retry after <n>s` means the token made too many requests (50 per second sustained,
bursts of 300, by default); wait for the `Retry-After` header's seconds. `413`
with `request body is too large` means the JSON-RPC body is over the API's body
cap (4 MiB by default).

### `405 method not allowed`, or the client can't connect

The endpoint accepts only `POST`. It implements the request/response (POST)
channel of MCP's Streamable HTTP transport, not a server-sent events stream over
`GET`. Use a client that supports Streamable HTTP, and point it at:

| Instance | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted | `https://mcp.flagon.io` (or `https://api.flagon.io/mcp`) |
| Self-hosted | `https://<your api host>/mcp`, or the root of your `FLAGON_MCP_HOST` |

### MCP changes happen without a confirmation step

Over MCP, Flagon runs a tool call when the client sends it: the proposal and
confirmation flow belongs to the in-product assistant. Most MCP clients ask you
before running a tool; check your client's settings. To limit what an agent can
do, give it a token with only the scopes it needs (read scopes only, for a
read-only agent).

## Related

- [Assistant](/docs/ai/assistant)
- [MCP](/docs/ai/mcp)
- [Tools](/docs/ai/tools)
- [Usage and AI limits](/docs/platform/usage)
- [AI safety](/docs/security/ai-safety)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.description: How to diagnose a problem in Flagon - read the status code and message, check the API's health routes and log - and where to find the fix for each kind of symptom.
docs.body:
When something goes wrong in Flagon, the answer is almost always already in the
response: a status code that names the category of problem and a message that
names the specific cause. This page shows where to find those, then points you to
the page for your symptom.

<Callout type="tip" title="Read the status first, then the message">

The HTTP status tells you what kind of problem it is (`401` who you are, `403`
what you may do, `404` what you can see, `409` a conflict with current state,
`413` a body that is too large, `422` invalid input, `429` too many requests,
`503` something not configured or not reachable). The message tells you which
rule you hit. Most problems are solved by those two lines alone.

</Callout>

## Match your symptom

| Symptom | Go to |
| --- | --- |
| You can't sign in, you're sent to a "Two-factor authentication required" or "Single sign-on required" page, or you see "Too many requests" | [Sign-in and SSO](/docs/troubleshooting/sign-in-and-sso) |
| An organization or project shows a 404, an action says you don't have permission, or a request says "this organization requires two-factor authentication" or "requires single sign-on" | [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions) |
| An API call returns an error status (including `429` "rate limit exceeded" or `413`) and you want to know the cause and fix | [API errors](/docs/troubleshooting/api-errors) |
| The assistant stops answering, answers with "mock mode", or an MCP client can't see or call a tool | [Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp) |
| You run your own instance and it exits at startup ("... is required in production"), can't reach its database, or the app can't reach the API | [Self-hosting issues](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues) |

## Where the information lives

### In the dashboard

Failed actions show the API's message inline (on a form or in a dialog). The app
passes the API's real status through its own route handlers, so a `403` from the
API is still a `403` in your browser's network tab, not a generic failure.

If a whole page fails to load, you see "We couldn't reach Flagon to load this
page." That means the app could not get an answer from the API; see
[the app can't reach the API](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues#the-app-cant-reach-the-api)
if you run your own instance.

### In API responses

Every REST error is a problem-details object (`application/problem+json`):

```json
{
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "this token is missing the scope required for this operation"
}
```

`detail` is the sentence to read, and it is always safe to show to a user.
Validation failures add an `errors` list naming each field. A `5xx` never
carries the internal cause: its `detail` is a short summary such as "could not
load profile", and the cause is in the API's log under the response's
`X-Request-Id`. The full shape is in
[Errors](/docs/api/errors), and each status with its causes is in
[API errors](/docs/troubleshooting/api-errors).

The MCP endpoint speaks JSON-RPC instead, so its failures come back as a JSON-RPC
`error` with a code and message, or as a tool result with `isError: true`. See
[Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp).

### On a self-hosted instance

Three routes on the API tell you its state, and none of them needs credentials:

```bash
curl -i https://api.example.com/healthz          # 200: the process is up
curl https://api.example.com/readyz              # 200 ok, or 503 "degraded" (cause in the log)
curl https://api.example.com/internal/rls-check  # 200 when tenant isolation is enforced
```

The API's log (JSON on stdout) records what it did at boot: whether it migrated,
which AI provider it picked, and any configuration it had to fall back from. See
[reading the API log](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues#reading-the-api-log).

## Still stuck

Collect the request you made, the status and `detail` you got back, the
`X-Request-Id` response header, and (on your own instance) the API's boot log and
the log lines carrying that `request_id`, then open an issue on the
[flagon-io/flagon](https://github.com/flagon-io/flagon) repository. Leave out
tokens, passwords, and connection strings.

## Related

- [API errors](/docs/troubleshooting/api-errors)
- [Errors](/docs/api/errors)
- [Self-hosting issues](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues)
- [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions)

docs.title: Self-hosting issues
docs.description: Diagnose a self-hosted Flagon instance - the API log, startup refusals in production mode, migration failures, database role and RLS errors, the app failing to reach the API, internal token mismatches, email, and build problems.
headings: The app role can't be provisioned
Password authentication fails for the app role
The app can't reach the API
`npm ci` fails on Linux with a missing native module
The app's Docker image fails to build
A Windows Firewall prompt every time the API starts
A `429` during local scripts or tests
docs.body:
A self-hosted instance has three moving parts that must agree with each other:
the API and its two database roles, the app and its database, and the shared
internal token between the app and the API. Almost every self-hosting problem is
one of those disagreeing. Start with the API's log and health routes, then find
your symptom below.

## Reading the API log

The API writes one JSON object per line to stdout. At boot it reports each step,
so the first few lines usually name the problem. Messages worth knowing:

| Message (`msg`) | Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `database setup complete` | info | `flagon-server migrate` finished. |
| `api listening` | info | The server is up, with the `addr` it bound. |
| `database unavailable; starting DEGRADED without migrations, /readyz will report it` | warn | Postgres did not answer after 6 attempts. The API serves, but `/readyz` returns `503`. |
| `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL not set; skipping app-role provisioning and grants (the runtime never falls back to the migrator role, so serving requires it)` | warn | `flagon-server migrate` ran without the app-role URL, so it did not provision the role. `serve` refuses to start without it in production. |
| `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN is not set; using the PUBLIC development token. Never expose this server to a network` | warn | Development mode with no internal token. Expected locally only. |
| `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEY is not set; stored credentials are encrypted with the PUBLIC development key, which is NOT secret. Set FLAGON_SECRETS_KEY before storing real SSO credentials` | warn | Development mode with no secrets key. Expected locally only. |
| `secrets encryption key loaded` | info | The secrets keyring is ready; `key_id` names the current key and `retired_key_ids` any keys from `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEYS_RETIRED`. |
| `encrypted stored credentials at rest under the current key` | info | The API sealed SSO secrets that were still plaintext or under a retired key; `rows` says how many. |
| `stored credentials: nothing left to re-seal under the current key` | info | Every stored SSO secret it could open is under the current key. After a rotation, and with no `could not open` warning, you can remove `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEYS_RETIRED`. |
| `could not open stored SSO secrets; leaving the row as is` | warn | An SSO secret was sealed with a key other than the current `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEY` or a retired one. Add the old key to `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEYS_RETIRED`, or enter that provider's secret again. |
| `mail provider is the LOG mailer in production: invitation emails are NOT delivered; set RESEND_API_KEY` | warn | Production without an email key. Invitations are created but not emailed. |
| `could not provision app role; runtime database access may fail` | warn | Creating or altering the app role failed. See [database role errors](#database-role-and-rls-errors). |
| `app role is managed by the database; leaving its password/attributes to the platform` | info | Your Postgres manages roles itself. Expected on some managed providers. |
| `could not grant runtime privileges to app role` | warn | The grants step failed; queries may fail with permission errors. |
| `AI agent enabled` | info | Which AI `provider` and `model` the assistant uses, and the `daily_limit`. |
| `AI provider is the offline MOCK (no model configured); set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (FLAGON_AI_BASE_URL) for real responses` | warn | No model is configured. See [Assistant and MCP](/docs/troubleshooting/assistant-and-mcp#the-assistant-answers-in-mock-mode). |
| `could not load docs corpus; documentation tools/endpoints disabled` | warn | The embedded docs failed to load; everything else serves. |
| `flagon exited with error` | error | A fatal error; the `err` field says which. |
| `internal error` | error | A request failed with a `5xx`. The `request_id` matches the response's `X-Request-Id` header, and `causes` holds the underlying error text that the response leaves out. |

## The API won't start

### "... is required in production"

The API decides at startup whether it runs in development or production mode. If
`FLAGON_ENV` is unset, it is production whenever it runs on Fly.io or binds
anything other than a loopback address (such as `FLAGON_HOST=0.0.0.0`, which the
API container image sets). Off Fly, the default `FLAGON_HOST` is `127.0.0.1`,
which is development. In production it refuses to start rather than fall back to
a public development value. The process exits with `flagon exited with error` and
one of these in `err`:

| `err` | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL is required in production (set FLAGON_ENV=development for local development)` | Set `DATABASE_URL`, or, on your own machine, put the API in development mode. |
| `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL is required in production: runtime queries must use the NOBYPASSRLS app role, never the migrator (set FLAGON_ENV=development for local development)` | Set `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL` to the app role. |
| `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN is required in production: set a long random secret shared with the app (set FLAGON_ENV=development for local development)` | Set `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the same random value on the API and the app. |
| `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN is set to the public development value; set a real secret in production` | Replace `dev-internal-token` with a real secret on both sides. |
| `FLAGON_SECRETS_KEY is required in production: set a base64-encoded 32-byte key (openssl rand -base64 32)` | Generate a key with `openssl rand -base64 32` and set it. |
| `invalid FLAGON_SECRETS_KEY: ...` | The value is not base64 or not 32 bytes. Generate a new one the same way. |
| `ai provider: FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ...`, `ai provider: FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER=openai requires ...`, or `ai provider: unknown FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER ...` | Set the pinned provider's key, fix the provider name, or unset `FLAGON_AI_PROVIDER` to fall back automatically. |
| `mail provider: FLAGON_MAIL_PROVIDER=resend requires RESEND_API_KEY` or `mail provider: unknown FLAGON_MAIL_PROVIDER ...` | Set the API's `RESEND_API_KEY`, or use `auto` or `log`. |

**Running locally and seeing the first one?** The API is in production mode
because it binds all interfaces, usually from a `FLAGON_HOST=0.0.0.0` in
`api/.env` or your shell. Remove it (the default is loopback), or set
`FLAGON_ENV=development`, and start it again. In containers, set
`FLAGON_ENV=development` for local stacks only, as the repository's compose file
does. Never set it on a server others can reach.

### Migration errors

If the database is reachable but migrating fails, the API exits with
`flagon exited with error` and an `err` that starts with
`database migration failed; refusing to start against a broken schema`. It
refuses on purpose: serving against a half-known schema is worse than not
serving. Nothing from the failed run is applied, because the run is one
transaction.

| `err` contains | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `was modified after being applied` ... `migrations are immutable once shipped` | A migration file that already ran against this database has changed (its checksum no longer matches `public.schema_migrations`). Usually a locally edited migration, or a build from a branch that rewrote one. | Restore the original file. Never edit an applied migration; add a new one. |
| `apply migration <name>` | That migration's SQL failed, followed by the Postgres error. | Read the Postgres error. Common causes are a migrator role that does not own the schema, or objects created by hand that conflict with the migration. |
| `acquire migration lock` | The migrator could not take the advisory lock. | Check that the migrator connection works and is not being cut by a proxy. |

To see the error without starting the server, run `flagon-server migrate`: it
performs the same setup and exits non-zero on failure.

### "database unavailable" and a 503 from /readyz

The API started degraded because it could not connect with `DATABASE_URL`.
`/readyz` answers `{"database":"unavailable","status":"degraded"}`; the reason is
in the API's log (`readiness check failed`, with the error). Check:

- The host and port are reachable **from where the API runs**. In a container,
  `localhost` is the container itself, not your machine.
- The credentials and database name. The API's `DATABASE_URL` points at
  `flagon_api`, not the app's `flagon_app`.
- The `sslmode` your server requires.

The API does not retry setup after boot. Once the database is back, restart the
API so it migrates.

## Database role and RLS errors

### The app role can't be provisioned

`could not provision app role` means the migrator could not create or alter the
role named in `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL`. The migrator needs permission to create
and alter roles (the compose file's `flagon` user and a standard Postgres
superuser can). If your provider does not allow that, create the role yourself:

```sql
CREATE ROLE flagon_app LOGIN PASSWORD '<password>'
  NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS;
```

Then restart the API; it grants the privileges on boot. If the grants step also
fails (`could not grant runtime privileges to app role`), grant `USAGE` on the
schemas and `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the `flagon_api` tables and
sequences through your provider. See [Database](/docs/self-hosting/database#how-the-api-provisions-the-app-role).

A warning that the role name is not a valid Postgres identifier, or that the URL
has no user or no password, means `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL` itself is malformed:
the role must be a plain identifier (letters, digits, underscores) and the URL
must include a password.

### Password authentication fails for the app role

The runtime pool connects as the app role. If Postgres rejects its password,
provisioning did not run or did not apply (check the log for the warnings
above), or your platform manages the role and its password differs from the one
in the URL. Make the URL match the role's real password.

### `/internal/rls-check` returns 503 or `"enforced":false`

The runtime role can see rows outside the organization bound to its transaction.
Tenant isolation is not in effect. The usual causes:

- `FLAGON_APP_DATABASE_URL` names a superuser or a role with `BYPASSRLS`, often
  the same user as `DATABASE_URL`. Use a separate, dedicated role.

A `503` whose body includes a `detail` field (`database unavailable`, or
`self-check query failed; see the server log`) means the check itself could not
run; it is not a verdict on isolation. The server log line `RLS self-check query
failed` carries the underlying error. Fix the
database connection and check again.

Fix the role and restart before letting users in.

## The app can't reach the API

**Symptom.** Pages show "We couldn't reach Flagon to load this page.", actions
fail with "The Flagon API is unreachable right now. Try again shortly.", and the
app's server log shows lines like `[flagon-api] GET /me unreachable`.

**What it means.** The app's server could not open a connection to
`FLAGON_API_URL` at all.

**How to fix.**

1. Check `FLAGON_API_URL` from the app's point of view. It is used server-side
   only, so it must resolve from the machine or container running the app. The
   default is `http://localhost:8080`.
2. Check that the API is listening (`api listening` in its log, and
   `curl <FLAGON_API_URL>/healthz` from the app's host).
3. Off Fly, the API binds `127.0.0.1` by default and only accepts connections
   from the same machine. Set `FLAGON_HOST=0.0.0.0` (as the API image does) when
   the app runs elsewhere or in another container, and set the production
   secrets, or `FLAGON_ENV=development` for a local stack.

## Internal token mismatch

**Symptom.** You can sign in, but every page that loads data fails, and the
API's answer is `401` with `invalid internal token`.

**What it means.** The app authenticates to the API with `FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN`,
and the two values differ. In development both sides fall back to
`dev-internal-token` when it is unset, so a mismatch there means one side has an
explicit value the other does not.

**How to fix.** Set the same value on both, or unset it on both in development.
In production, generate a long random value and set it on both processes.
Restart both.

A production app (`NODE_ENV=production`) with no token fails every API call with
`FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN is required in production (it must match the API's FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN).`
in its server log, and the seed script, when run with `NODE_ENV=production` and
no token, prints `Skipped demo org: FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN is not set.`

If the API answers `503` with `identity API is not configured`, the API itself has
no internal token. A current API cannot start in production that way, so check
which binary and configuration you are running.

## Emails are not delivered

Two processes send email. The app sends verification codes and password resets;
the API sends invitations.

- **Locally**, without `RESEND_API_KEY`, the app does not send email: it prints
  each message (including verification codes) to its console as
  `[email] to <address> - <subject>`. Copy the code from there. The API likewise
  logs invitation emails as `[email] not sent (log mailer)`, with the text
  (including the accept link) in the `text` field. Those invitations report
  `email_sent: false`, and the dashboard's invite dialog shows the link to copy.
- **Invitations never arrive in production.** The API needs its own
  `RESEND_API_KEY` (and `FLAGON_MAIL_FROM` on a verified domain); the app's key is
  not shared with it. At boot the API warns
  `mail provider is the LOG mailer in production: invitation emails are NOT delivered; set RESEND_API_KEY`.
  If the links in invitation emails point at the wrong host, set `FLAGON_APP_URL`
  to your app's public URL.
- **In production**, a missing key is an error:
  `RESEND_API_KEY is not set: refusing to drop a transactional email in production.`
  Set the key.
- `Resend send failed (<status>): ...` means Resend rejected the message. The
  most common cause is a `RESEND_FROM` address on a domain you have not verified
  with Resend.

## The app's database

- The app connects to `flagon_app` with its own `DATABASE_URL`. If that variable
  holds the API's URL by mistake, sign-in fails because the auth tables are not
  there.
- Unless the URL says `sslmode=disable`, the app verifies the database's TLS
  certificate fully. A self-signed certificate fails until Node trusts it.
- A build that prints
  `WARNING: DATABASE_URL is not set; skipping migrations. Auth will not work until it is configured.`
  skipped the auth migrations. Set `DATABASE_URL` and run
  `npm run db:migrate --workspace app`.

## Build and install problems

### `npm ci` fails on Linux with a missing native module

An error such as `Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'` means
`package-lock.json` is missing the entries for that platform's native binaries.
npm records them based on the platform that resolved the lockfile, and `npm ci`
installs only what the lockfile lists. Regenerate a complete, cross-platform
lockfile (requires Docker) and commit it:

```bash
scripts/relock.sh
```

### The app's Docker image fails to build

If `docker build` on `app/Dockerfile` fails with `"/package-lock.json": not found`,
the build context is wrong. The app is an npm workspace whose lockfile lives at
the repository root, so build from the root:

```bash
docker build -f app/Dockerfile .
```

The compose file already uses the root as the app's build context. See
[Installation](/docs/self-hosting/installation#run-the-app-with-docker).

### Port already in use locally

`compose.override.yml` publishes the compose API on `8080` and the compose app
on `4000`. If you run the API or app natively, comment out that service's
`ports` in your `compose.override.yml` so the native server can bind the port.

### A Windows Firewall prompt every time the API starts

The API binds loopback (`127.0.0.1`) by default, which the firewall does not
prompt for. If you still get the prompt, remove any `FLAGON_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or
empty `FLAGON_HOST`) override from `api/.env` or your shell.

### A `429` during local scripts or tests

The API rate limits each principal (50 requests per second, bursts of 300, by
default) and answers `429` with `rate limit exceeded; retry after <n>s` beyond
that. For bulk local work, raise `FLAGON_RATE_LIMIT` and `FLAGON_RATE_BURST`, or
set `FLAGON_RATE_LIMIT=0` to turn the limiter off on your machine.

### Starting over locally

`docker compose down -v` deletes the Postgres volume, and with it both
databases, including every local account. Afterwards run `docker compose up -d postgres`,
start the API (it migrates on boot), then `npm run db:migrate --workspace app`
and `npm run db:seed --workspace app`.

## Related

- [Installation](/docs/self-hosting/installation)
- [Database](/docs/self-hosting/database)
- [Production](/docs/self-hosting/production)
- [Configuration](/docs/self-hosting/configuration)
- [API errors](/docs/troubleshooting/api-errors)

docs.title: Sign-in and SSO
docs.description: Fixes for email verification, two-factor codes, sign-in rate limits, the two-factor and single sign-on requirement pages, SSO provider errors, and deleted accounts.
headings: "Too many requests. Please try again later."
"This account has been deleted. Contact support to restore it."
docs.body:
Sign-in is handled by the Flagon app (the web UI), using BetterAuth for
passwords, email codes, two-factor authentication, social sign-in, and
organization single sign-on (SSO). Organizations can then add their own
requirements on top: two-factor for every member, or sign-in through the
organization's identity provider. This page walks through each place sign-in can
stop you and what to do.

## Your email isn't verified

<Callout type="warn" title="Signing in sends you to a verification page">

You enter a correct email and password, and instead of the dashboard you land on
the email verification page.

</Callout>

**What it means.** Every account must verify its email before it can sign in.
When sign-in is refused because the address is unverified, the app routes you to
verification. If you signed in with a username, the page asks for your email
first.

**How to fix.**

1. Enter the code from the verification email, or click the link in it. Verifying
   signs you in.
2. If the link says "That link didn't work or expired. Enter the code below
   instead.", request a fresh code on the page and type it in.
3. If no email arrives, check spam. On a self-hosted instance, see
   [emails are not delivered](/docs/troubleshooting/self-hosting-issues#emails-are-not-delivered).

Password reset links work the same way and expire after one hour; request a new
one if yours is older.

## "Too many requests. Please try again later."

<Callout type="warn" title="Sign-in, sign-up, or a code request fails with 429">

The form shows "Too many requests. Please try again later." and the request
returned `429 Too Many Requests`.

</Callout>

**What it means.** The auth endpoints are rate limited per client to stop
password guessing, code brute-forcing, and email flooding. The limits, per
60-second window:

| Action | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Sign up | 5 requests |
| Send a verification code | 3 requests |
| Verify an email code | 10 requests |
| Request a password reset | 3 requests |
| Reset a password | 10 requests |
| Any other auth request (including sign-in) | 20 requests |

**How to fix.** Wait. The response carries an `X-Retry-After` header with the
number of seconds until the window resets. The counters are stored in the app's
database, so they apply across every app instance and a different browser tab
does not reset them.

## Two-factor codes don't work

**What it means.** If your account has two-factor authentication (2FA), a correct
password takes you to a second step that asks for a 6-digit code from your
authenticator app. "That code didn't work. Try again." means the code was wrong
or expired.

**How to fix.**

1. Check that your device's clock is set automatically. Authenticator codes are
   time-based, and a drifting clock produces codes the server rejects.
2. Use the newest code, not one that is about to roll over.
3. Lost your device? Switch to **backup code** on the same page and enter one of
   the codes you saved when you enabled 2FA. Each backup code works once.

## "Two-factor authentication required"

<Callout type="warn" title="Opening an organization sends you to a two-factor page">

You are signed in, but opening the organization shows "Two-factor
authentication required" with a **Set up two-factor** button.

</Callout>

**What it means.** An owner or admin of that organization turned on **Require
two-factor authentication** (Settings, then Security, then Authentication), and
your account does not have 2FA enabled. Your other organizations and your
personal settings still work.

**How to fix.**

1. Choose **Set up two-factor**, which opens your personal
   [security settings](/docs/platform/two-factor) at `/settings/security`, and
   enable it.
2. Return and choose **I've enabled it - continue**.

If you are the admin trying to turn the requirement on and the switch is
disabled, the page explains why: enable 2FA on your own account first, so turning
the requirement on cannot lock you out. The API enforces the same rule, answering
`403` "enable two-factor authentication on your own account before requiring it
for the organization" if the change is attempted anyway.

The requirement is enforced by the API as well as by this page, so scripts using
your personal access token, the assistant, and MCP clients get `403` for that
organization until you enable 2FA. See
[Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions).

## "Single sign-on required"

<Callout type="warn" title="Opening an organization sends you to a single sign-on page">

You are signed in, but opening the organization shows "Single sign-on required"
with a **Continue with SSO** button.

</Callout>

**What it means.** The organization requires members to sign in through its
identity provider, and your current session was not established through one of
its providers (for example, you signed in with a password or another
organization's SSO). Organization **owners** are exempt, so an owner can always
reach settings to fix or turn off SSO.

**How to fix.**

1. Choose **Continue with SSO** and complete sign-in at your identity provider.
   You come back signed in to the same Flagon account, with the organization's
   SSO identity linked to it, even if the identity provider uses a different
   email address.
2. If the page says "No SSO provider is configured for this organization yet.
   Contact an owner.", the requirement is on but no provider exists. Only an
   owner can fix that, by adding a provider or turning the requirement off.

The API applies the same rule to every request for the organization, so a
personal access token also gets `403` until you have signed in through one of the
organization's providers at least once. See
[Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions).

## SSO sign-in fails

**"Single sign-on is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly."** Before every
SSO sign-in, the app refreshes the provider's settings from the Flagon API, and
it fails closed when it cannot. The API was unreachable or refused the app. Try
again; on your own instance, check that the app can reach the API and that
`FLAGON_INTERNAL_TOKEN` matches on both sides.

**"No SSO provider is configured for that email domain."** Signing in with
**Sign in with SSO** looks up the provider by the domain of the email you type.
Check the address, or ask an organization owner which domain the provider is
registered for.

**The identity provider shows an error before sending you back.** This is almost
always a mismatch between what the provider expects and what Flagon sends. Check
that the provider has the exact callback URL for your provider ID:

| Protocol | URL to register at the identity provider |
| --- | --- |
| OIDC | `https://<app host>/api/auth/sso/callback/<providerId>` |
| SAML | ACS URL `https://<app host>/api/auth/sso/saml2/sp/acs/<providerId>` |

Also confirm the issuer, client ID and secret (OIDC) or entry point and signing
certificate (SAML) in the organization's SSO settings. Changes made there take
effect on the next sign-in. See [Set up SSO with OIDC](/docs/guides/set-up-sso-oidc)
and [Set up SSO with SAML](/docs/guides/set-up-sso-saml).

**SAML works locally but not in production, or the reverse.** SAML posts its
response back to the app from the identity provider's site. In production the app
issues its session cookie with `SameSite=None; Secure` so that post carries your
session, which requires HTTPS end to end.

## "This account has been deleted. Contact support to restore it."

**What it means.** The account was deleted, which blocks every way of signing in.
The account is soft-deleted, so it can be restored.

**How to fix.** Contact support for the hosted service. On your own instance, an
operator can restore it from the app directory:

```bash
npm run restore-user --workspace app -- someone@example.com --dry-run   # preview
npm run restore-user --workspace app -- someone@example.com
```

## Social sign-in buttons are disabled

Google and GitHub sign-in buttons are always shown, and are enabled only when
the instance has credentials for that provider. On your own instance, set
`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` (or the `GITHUB_` pair) and rebuild
the app; the enabled state is decided at build time.

## Related

- [Two-factor authentication](/docs/platform/two-factor)
- [Single sign-on](/docs/platform/sso)
- [Require two-factor](/docs/guides/require-two-factor)
- [Access and permissions](/docs/troubleshooting/access-and-permissions)
